    "text": "# How to Integrate AI into a Chrome Extension: A Developer's Guide to Building Intelligent Browser Tools\n\nChrome extensions have long been the go-to tool for enhancing user productivity, customizing web experiences, and automating repetitive tasks. But in 2025, the real game-changer is this: **AI-powered Chrome extensions**. By integrating artificial intelligence directly into the browser experience, developers can build powerful assistants for writing, research, summarization, communication, image recognition, and more.\n\nIn this article, we’ll break down exactly how developers can incorporate AI into their Chrome extensions, the architectural patterns that work best, and real-world use cases to inspire your next build.\n\n## Why Build AI-Powered Chrome Extensions?\n\nChrome extensions are ideal AI wrappers for a few reasons:\n\n- They’re **lightweight**, fast to deploy, and often have viral growth loops.\n\n- Users stay in the browser — no need to switch tabs or apps.\n\n- They integrate deeply into the user’s **web workflow** (Gmail, LinkedIn, Google Docs, etc.)\n\n- With AI, they go from helpful to **transformational**.\n\n\nExamples of successful AI-powered extensions include Grammarly, Jasper Everywhere, Glasp, and Compose AI — all of which provide real-time enhancements using NLP, summarization, or generation.\n\n## 3 Ways to Integrate AI into a Chrome Extension\n\n### 1\\. **API-based AI (e.g. OpenAI, Claude, Gemini)**\n\nThis is the most common approach. You call an AI model hosted remotely (via HTTP) and return the result to the user.\n\n**Use Case:** Improve selected text with GPT **Tech Stack:** Content script → background script → API call → display result\n\n### 2\\. **Local ML Models with TensorFlow.js**\n\nFor privacy-focused or offline use cases, you can run small models in the browser using TensorFlow.js or ONNX.js.\n\n**Use Case:** Sentiment analysis of a webpage **Tech Stack:** Content script loads TensorFlow model, runs predictions in-browser.\n\n### 3\\. **AI Backend + Extension Frontend**\n\nBuild your own backend using LangChain, Hugging Face pipelines, or a custom PyTorch/LLM stack. The extension becomes a UI for hitting custom endpoints.\n\n**Use Case:** Legal document analyzer, custom search agent **Benefit:** Full control over models, workflows, prompt chaining, and memory.\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n**Typical AI flow:**\n\n1. User selects text or opens extension\n\n2. Extension sends input to AI model (API or local)\n\n3. Receives response\n\n4. Injects result into DOM or displays in popup\n\n\n## Common AI Use Cases in Extensions\n\n## Considerations and Best Practices\n\n- **Secure your API keys:** Never store them in the frontend. Use a proxy backend if needed.",

    "text": "If you’ve searched for the best Chrome to-do list or browser-based task manager, you’ve probably noticed a pattern: most tools are overcomplicated.\n[ToDo - Keep it Simple](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/todo-keep-it-simple/gphopdfofabeiklbccfndgeempbfodhc)\n\nWhen I needed a simple way to manage tasks directly in my browser, every option I tried had the same problems:\n\n1️⃣Overloaded with features I didn’t need.\n\n2️⃣Forced account sign-ups.\n\n3️⃣Distracting, cluttered interfaces.\n\nSo, I built my own.\n\nWhy Most Chrome To-Do List Extensions Fail\nDon’t get me wrong — productivity tools are powerful.           <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "text": "Manifest V3 migration guide | Firefox Extension Workshop\n### [Extension Workshop](https://extensionworkshop.com/)\nSearch[Submit or Manage Extensions](https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addons)\nSearch\n# Manifest V3 migration guide\nManifest V3 became generally available in Firefox 109 after being available as a developer preview from Firefox 101. This page details what's changed and how you adapt your extensions to take advantage of Manifest V3.\nSee the[Developing extensions for Firefox for Android](https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/developing-extensions-for-firefox-for-android/#mv3-compatibility)page for additional guidance if you plan to support Firefox for Android.\n###### Contents\n1. [What is Manifest V3?](#what-is-manifest-v3)\n2. [Manifest V3 changes](#developer-preview-changes)\n3. [Migration checklist](#migration-checklist)\n## What is Manifest V3?\nManifest V3 (MV3) is the umbrella term for several foundational changes to the WebExtensions API in Firefox. The name refers to the declared`manifest\\_version`key in each extension’s[manifest.json](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json)file.\nThe Manifest V3 changes apply to extensions for Safari, Firefox, and Chromium-based browsers –such as Chrome, Edge, and Opera. While the goal is to maintain a high degree of compatibility between the Firefox, Safari, and Chromium extension platforms, our implementation diverges where we think it matters and where our values point to a different direction.\nThis article discusses the changes introduced with Manifest V3 in Firefox and highlights where they diverge from the Chrome and Safari implementation.\n## Manifest V3 changes\nThis section details the Manifest V3 changes made to Firefox.\n### Manifest version\nThe manifest.json key[`manifest\\_version`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/manifest_version)accepts`3`. To use Manifest V3, update your manifest.json file like this:\n```\n`\"manifest\\_version\":3`\n```\n### Search extensions icons\nSearch extensions must use local icons. This change prevents the unnecessary network pings that result from accessing remote icons.\nTo accommodate this change, provide a local icon and define it in your manifest.json[chrome\\_settings\\_overrides](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/chrome_settings_overrides)manifest key like this:\n```",

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Context7_resolve-library-id**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Context7 - resolve-library-id: Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'query-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

*Parameters*:
  * libraryName: chrome extension starter
  * query: Best modern frontend framework and starter for Chrome extension development in 2026

*Result*:
Available Libraries:

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "text": "## What is CRXJS?\n\nCRXJS Vite Plugin is a tool that helps you make Chrome Extensions using modern\nweb development technology.\n\nThings like **HMR** and **static asset imports** work out of the box so you can\nget started making a modern Chrome Extension, not configuring build tools.\n\ntip\n\nWe have getting started guides for the following frameworks:\n\n### [React](https://crxjs.dev/vite-plugin/getting-started/react/create-project) [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#react-logo-react)\n\n### [Solid](https://crxjs.dev/vite-plugin/getting-started/solid/create-project) [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#solid-logo-solid)\n\n### [Vanilla JavaScript](https://crxjs.dev/vite-plugin/getting-started/vanilla-js/create-project) [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#js-logo-vanilla-javascript)\n\n### [Vue](https://crxjs.dev/vite-plugin/getting-started/vue/create-project) [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#vue-logo-vue)\n\nThe first two sections for any framework only take 90 seconds to complete.\n\n## Why CRXJS? [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#why-crxjs)\n\nWe've grown to expect a **polished developer experience** these days. Build\ntools like Create React App or Vite make it easy to start making a web app.\nUnfortunately, building a Chrome Extension isn't the same.\n\nYou crawl the web looking for the perfect boilerplate, and the most popular ones\naren't that simple or don't support more than one framework. When it's time to\nadd another extension page or content script, you have to update your config in\nmore than one place, and nice things like true HMR for content scripts are hard\nto come by.\n\nNot anymore. CRXJS Vite Plugin simplifies the Chrome Extension developer\nexperience by combining the refined features of Vite with a simple configuration\nstrategy:\n\n## Use the manifest! [​](http://crxjs.dev/crxjs.dev\\#use-the-manifest)\n\nCRXJS parses `manifest.json` to find the files to include in your extension. The\nmanifest is the central document that declares most of the files and\nconfiguration for your extension, why do we need more?\n\nHelp wanted\n\nThese docs are a work in progress! We are adding new content every week. If you\nhave questions or ideas, please\n[join the discussion on GitHub](https://github.com/crxjs/chrome-extension-tools/discussions)\nor make a PR.",

开发谷歌浏览器（Chrome）扩展插件是一个非常棒的前端实践方向。由于你明确要求**纯前端（无后端）**，我们的重心将放在利用浏览器原生 API（如 `chrome.storage`、`chrome.tabs`、`chrome.scripting` 等）和现代前端技术栈（Vite + React/Vue + TypeScript）上。

以下我为你策划的几个具有实用价值且适合纯前端实现的创意方向，以及建议的技术栈：

### 1. 创意方向：解决实际痛点

#### A. 效率提升类 (Productivity)
*   **"Tab Stash" 标签页暂存器**：类似 OneTab，但在 UI 上做创新。允许用户将当前窗口的所有标签页一键“打包”存入本地（`chrome.storage.local`），并支持分类、搜索和导出 Markdown 格式的链接列表。
*   **"Focus Mode" 定制化屏蔽器**：允许用户预设“专注模式”，开启后自动重定向（Redirect）或隐藏特定干扰网站的 DOM 元素（如 B站的推荐列表、知乎的热榜），纯前端即可通过 `declarativeNetRequest` 或 Content Scripts 实现。

#### B. 开发者工具类 (Developer Utilities)
*   **"API Mocker" 前端模拟器**：拦截特定的网络请求并返回自定义的 JSON 数据。这对于前端开发调试非常有用，完全可以在扩展插件内通过 `chrome.debugger` 或 `declarativeNetRequest` 动态修改响应。
*   **"Snippet Manager" 代码片段管家**：在侧边栏（Side Panel）提供一个快速查找和复制常用代码片段、正则表达式、常用颜色值的工具，支持同步到谷歌账号（`chrome.storage.sync`）。

#### C. 内容增强类 (Content Enhancement)
*   **"Zen Reader" 禅意阅读器**：自动识别网页正文并重新排版，支持自定义字体、间距、背景色（护眼模式），并提供本地化的阅读进度标记。
*   **"Web Annotator" 网页划线笔**：允许在任意网页上划线、写批注，这些数据保存在本地。再次访问该网页时，通过 Content Script 自动还原高亮效果。

#### D. AI 辅助类 (Local AI Wrapper)
*   **"Local Summarizer" 网页摘要**：利用 Chrome 浏览器 2024/2025 年新推出的内置 AI API（如 `window.ai`）或者集成简单的 Hugging Face Transformers.js（在浏览器运行小模型），实现纯本地化的网页总结。

---

### 2. 建议技术栈 (Skills & Stack)

为了让你的开发体验达到 2026 年的主流水平，建议采用以下组合：

*   **构建工具**：**Vite** + **CRXJS (Vite Plugin)**。这是目前开发扩展体验最好的方案，支持热更新（HMR），且能自动处理 `manifest.json`。
*   **框架**：**React 19** 或 **Vue 3**。
*   **语言**：**TypeScript**（必选，扩展 API 的类型定义非常丰富，能极大减少 Bug）。
*   **样式**：**Tailwind CSS** + **shadcn/ui**。可以快速做出极具现代感的 UI。
*   **存储**：使用 `chrome.storage.local`（持久化）或 `IndexedDB`（处理大数据）。

---

### 3. 开发建议：快速起步

如果你想现在就开始，可以尝试以下步骤：

1.  **环境搭建**：
    使用成熟的脚手架快速生成项目结构：
    ```bash
    npx create-vite my-extension --template react-ts
    ```
    并安装 `crxjs`：
    ```bash
    npm i @crxjs/vite-plugin@beta -D
    ```

2.  **核心文件**：
    *   `manifest.json`：配置插件的权限（Permissions）和入口（Popup/SidePanel/Background）。
    *   `popup.html`：点击插件图标弹出的界面。
    *   `content_scripts`：注入到网页中运行的代码，用于修改网页 DOM。
    *   `background.js` (Service Worker)：处理浏览器级别的事件（如快捷键、右键菜单）。

3.  **遵循 Manifest V3 标准**：
    确保你的插件符合谷歌最新的 **Manifest V3** 规范，这是目前发布到 Web Store 的唯一标准。

**你对以上哪个方向最感兴趣？或者你希望我针对某个特定的技术细节（比如如何实现划线保存）提供更深入的指导？**

          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "text": "Using local storage for high scores and game progress - Gamedev.js\n[![Gamedev.js](https://gamedevjs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/gamedevjs-com-website-banner-2.png)](https://gamedevjs.com/)\n* [News](https://gamedevjs.com/)\n* [Shop](https://gamedevjs.com/shop)\n* [Jam](https://gamedevjs.com/jam)\n* [Survey](https://gamedevjs.com/survey)\n* [Newsletter](https://gamedevjsweekly.com/)\n* [Contact](https://gamedevjs.com/contact/)\n* [Join](https://gamedevjs.com/join/)\n**\nMenu\n[Home](https://gamedevjs.com/)**[Articles](https://gamedevjs.com/category/articles/)**Using local storage for high scores and game progress\n# Using local storage for high scores and game progress\n* [Articles](https://gamedevjs.com/category/articles/)\n[20th January 2023](https://gamedevjs.com/articles/using-local-storage-for-high-scores-and-game-progress/)\n**0\n**15299\n![](https://gamedevjs.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/basics-localstorage-728x485.jpg)\n**Local storage**is a powerful feature of HTML5 that allows developers to store key-value pairs in the browser, even after the browser is closed. This makes it an ideal way to save game progress and high scores in HTML5 games.\nTo use local storage in JavaScript, you first need to check if the browser supports it. You can do this by using the[localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage)object and checking if it is`null`. If the browser supports it, you can then use the[setItem](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage/setItem)method to store a key-value pair and the[getItem](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage/getItem)method to retrieve the value associated with a key.\nHere&#8217;s an example of how you can use local storage to save the player&#8217;s current score in a game:\n```\n`// Check if the browser supports local storage\nif(localStorage) {\n// Save the current score to local storage\nlocalStorage.setItem(\"currentScore\", score);\n}`\n```\nAnd then, to retrieve the score:\n```\n`// Check if the browser supports local storage\nif(localStorage) {\n// Retrieve the current score from local storage\nvar score = localStorage.getItem(\"currentScore\");\n}`\n```\nTo save the game progress, you can use a similar approach, but instead of storing a single value, you would need to store the entire game state. One way to do this would be to convert the game state to a JSON string using`JSON.stringify()`, and then store that string in local storage.\n```\n`// Check if the browser supports local storage\nif(localStorage) {\n// Convert the game state to a JSON string\nvar gameState = JSON.stringify(state);\n// Save the game state to local storage\nlocalStorage.setItem(\"gameState\", gameState);\n}`\n```\nAnd then, to retrieve the game state:\n```\n`// Check if the browser supports local storage",

    "text": "How to Save High Scores in Local Storage\n[](/)\n[Michael Karén&#x27;s Blog](/?source=top_nav_blog_home)\nFollow\n[Michael Karén&#x27;s Blog](/?source=top_nav_blog_home)\nFollow\n[](https://twitter.com/melcor76)[](https://github.com/melcor76)[](https://michaelkaren.dev/)[](https://hashnode.com/@melcor76)[](/rss.xml)\n![How to Save High Scores in Local Storage](https://cdn.hashnode.com/res/hashnode/image/upload/v1618075280966/Hc3wuf1J_.jpeg?w=1600&amp;h=840&amp;fit=crop&amp;crop=entropy&amp;auto=compress,format&amp;format=webp)\n# How to Save High Scores in Local Storage\n[![](data:image/svg+xml,%3csvg%20xmlns=%27http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%27%20version=%271.1%27%20width=%27200%27%20height=%27200%27/%3e)![Michael Karén&#x27;s photo](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7)](https://hashnode.com/@melcor76)\n[Michael Karén](https://hashnode.com/@melcor76)\n·[Jan 11, 2021](https://blog.michaelkaren.dev/how-to-save-high-scores-in-local-storage-7860baca9d68)·\n5min read\nAfter creating a game, it would be nice to save our best scores. If we only save the score in memory it will be gone the next time we play. Instead, we can save the scores in the browser’s local storage.\nThis article steps through how to save high scores in local storage and then how to present them on the screen for the player. If you want to read about the game that inspired this article you can read about it here:\n* [Learning Modern JavaScript with Tetris](https://medium.com/@michael.karen/learning-modern-javascript-with-tetris-92d532bcd057)## Local storage\nWith local storage, we can store data in the browser in the form of key-value pairs, where both the key and the value are strings. The data is persisted across browser sessions and its scope is limited to the origin where the script that accesses local storage resides.\nDifferent browsers use different storages, so data is not shared between different browsers on the same computer —each browser has its unique storage.\nThe following snippets show how we can use localStorage:\n```\n`// Add datalocalStorage.setItem('myCar','Tesla');// Read dataconstcar =localStorage.getItem('myCar');// Remove specific datalocalStorage.removeItem('myCar');// Remove all datalocalStorage.clear();`\n```\nWith this knowledge, we can start implementing our solution.\n## Load high scores\nLet’s start by defining a couple of constants:\n```\n`constNO\\_OF\\_HIGH\\_SCORES =10;constHIGH\\_SCORES ='highScores';`\n```\nSince we want to store an array we need to translate the array into a string before we save it and back to an array when getting it. For this, we can use the*JSON object*that contains methods for parsing JSON and converting values to JSON.\nWe can parse the string that we get from localStorage. If we don’t have any scores saved yet we can use the OR operator`||`to give a default value of empty array:\n```\n`consthighScoreString =localStorage.getItem(HIGH\\_SCORES);consthighScores =JSON.parse(highScoreString) || [];`\n```\nWe now have the high scores parsed into an array. Next, we need to check if a score is good enough to make the high score list.\n## Check for a high score\nTo get the lowest score on the list we can take the score from the last position in the array with the help of our constant`NO\\_OF\\_HIGH\\_SCORES`. If we don’t have a full list yet we can use optional chaining with the Elvis operator (?) and return a zero:\n```\n`constlowestScore = highScores[NO\\_OF\\_HIGH\\_SCORES —1]?.score ??0;`\n```\nWe have enough now to create a function`checkHighScore()`:\n```\n`functioncheckHighScore(score){consthighScores =JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(HIGH\\_SCORES)) || [];constlowestScore = highScores[NO\\_OF\\_HIGH\\_SCORES -1]?.score ??0;if(score &gt; lowestScore) {",

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

做“小游戏集合”确实是一个更有趣、互动性更强的方向！在 Chrome 扩展中做游戏，最大的优势是**触手可及**——用户可以在刷网页、等代码编译或开会间隙，随手点开侧边栏（Side Panel）或弹出框（Popup）玩一把。

结合 2026 年的技术趋势，以下是几个更具“生命力”的小游戏集合创意方向：

### 1. 核心创意：让游戏融入浏览体验

#### 方向 A：SidePanel 游戏盒子 (SidePanel GameHub)
利用 Chrome 最新的 **Side Panel API**。
*   **概念**：将游戏放在侧边栏。侧边栏的优势在于**持久化**——当你切换标签页时，侧边栏不会关闭。
*   **有趣点**：可以做成一个“摸鱼盒子”，包含扫雷、数独、2048 等经典小游戏的极简版。
*   **纯前端玩法**：使用 `chrome.storage.local` 跨游戏保存积分和成就系统，做一个“本地排行榜”。

#### 方向 B：网页元素“粉碎机” (Web Element Destroyer)
这是一种基于 **Content Scripts** 的交互游戏。
*   **概念**：玩家点击插件图标，当前网页变成关卡。
*   **有趣点**：你可以用一个“小飞机”或“激光笔”去射击网页上的 DOM 元素（按钮、图片、文字段落），击碎它们获得分数。
*   **纯前端技术**：通过 Content Script 注入 Canvas 层，或者直接用 CSS 动画处理 DOM 的消失效果。

#### 方向 C：标签页“电子宠物” (Tab Pet)
*   **概念**：在侧边栏或网页角落养一只“代码猿”或“摸鱼猫”。
*   **有趣点**：它的成长取决于你的浏览行为。比如你打开 StackOverflow 的次数多，它会变聪明；你开的标签页太多（超过 20 个），它会表现得很焦虑甚至在网页上跑来跑去提醒你关标签。
*   **纯前端玩法**：利用 `chrome.tabs.onCreated` 等 API 监听浏览器行为，驱动宠物的状态机。

#### 方向 D：Idle/Clicker 挂机游戏 (The Idle Browser)
*   **概念**：利用浏览器作为“发电机”。
*   **有趣点**：只要浏览器开着，你就在收集“流量点数”。你可以用点数升级你的“虚拟服务器”，购买更好的“防火墙”。
*   **纯前端玩法**：利用 `chrome.alarms` 定时离线收益，即使你没打开插件界面，后台也在模拟运行。

---

### 2. 为什么“小游戏集合”适合你？

1.  **纯前端友好**：不需要服务器。游戏逻辑、图形渲染（Canvas/SVG）和数据保存（local storage）全部在浏览器端完成。
2.  **易于扩展**：你可以先做一个游戏（比如贪吃蛇），然后像乐高一样不断往里加新模块。
3.  **视觉反馈强**：作为前端开发者，你可以充分发挥 CSS 动画、Canvas 绘图的功底。

---

### 3. 进阶玩法建议 (Skills Upgrade)

*   **使用 PixiJS 或 Phaser**：如果你想做更复杂一点的 2D 效果，这两个库在纯前端环境下非常强大且轻量。
*   **接入 Chrome 内置 AI (window.ai)**：让 AI 根据当前网页的内容生成游戏关卡。例如：如果网页是关于“烹饪”的，小游戏就自动切换成“切菜”模式。
*   **本地对战**：通过 `postMessage` 实现两个标签页之间的“分屏”对战。

---

### 4. 你的第一步

你可以先尝试做一个 **"SidePanel 极简游戏盒子"**：
1.  在 `manifest.json` 中声明 `side_panel` 权限。
2.  配置一个 `default_path` 指向你的 `index.html`。
3.  在里面先塞入一个你最拿手的 JavaScript 游戏（比如 2048）。

**你觉得哪种形式的游戏更吸引你？是想做一个常驻侧边栏的安静盒子，还是一个能和网页元素互动的狂野工具？**

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

*Parameters*:
  * query: most unique innovative browser extensions art digital gardens meta-games

    "uri": "https://wikibonsai.io/",
    "text": "WikiBonsai\n[![Logo](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/wikibonsai-light.svg)](https://wikibonsai.io/)\nWikiBonsai\n# a jungle gym for thought,\n# with an API for the mind.\nWikiBonsai is a methodology and set of tools that\nnudge note-taking toward meaningful mind-training\nKnowledge BonsaiConsult\n# 🪨Bedrock Workflows\nThe WikiBonsai project transforms a collection of markdown files into a text-based, easy-to-navigate, jungle gym for thought with an API for the mind. This is accomplished by enabling specific personal knowledge management (PKM) workflows:\n## Concept Webs\nExtend markdown with`[[wikirefs]]`for quick associative linking\n## Semantic Trees\nCultivate and train a unified knowledge bonsai across a collection of markdown files\n## Attribute Metadata\nDefines`:semantic::attributes`for clean, lean, yaml-like structured data\n## Memory Palaces\nExperience and interact with a unified visual-spatial representation that emerges from the relationships formed across markdown notes\n# 🌱Tools for Growing\nGrow your knowledge base with the help of AI-generated seedlings and training: Starter-seedlings can help kick off the process of conceptual analysis whether you're new to that topic or an old-hand looking for a reference. And tree-training can illuminate underlying structures in order to improve your writing and thinking.\n![germinator](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/germinator.svg)\nCome with me if you want togrow\n![tree-trainer](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/tree-trainer.png)\nInside you have strong root. No need nothing except what inside you togrow\n# ✂️Tools for Tending\nWith WikiBonsai workflows, a collection of notes or a wiki is transformed into a unified, growing collection and taking notes becomes synonymous with gardening -- whose results will surely bear fruit. Tending your markdown digital garden is possible from...\n[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tendr-cli/)...the CLI[](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=manunamz.vscode-tendr)...an IDE\n[![vscode-tendr](https://wikibonsai.io/img/demo-vscode-tendr.png)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=manunamz.vscode-tendr)\n# 💐Tools for Showcasing\nBy simply turning on WikiBonsai workflows, you can extend a blog, publish a wiki, or simply showcase what you've cultivated with your favorite static site generator.\n[![astro-bloomz](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/Astro.svg)](https://astro-bloomz.netlify.app)[![eleventy-bloomz](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/eleventy-logo.svg)](https://eleventy-bloomz.netlify.app)[![jekyll-bloomz](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/jekyll.png)](https://jekyll-bloomz.netlify.app)[![jekyll-garden](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/jekyll-plus.svg)](https://jekyll-garden.netlify.app)\n# ✨Tools for Tinkering\n[![oss](https://wikibonsai.io/img/logo/oss.svg)](https://github.com/wikibonsai/)\nThis project is about strategically implementing and open-sourcing functionality that will benefit the most users and developers across the digital ecosystem. Thus, it abides by the Unix Philosophy: Everything is modularized and implemented in such a way as to maximize re-use whether it be for the browser, desktop, mobile, or headset. It&#39;s about furthering the state of PKM as a whole by building atop[&quot;standardization bedrock&quot;](https://github.com/wikibonsai/wikibonsai/tree/main/docs/DESIGN.md#drilling-down-to-standardization-bedrock)instead of just creating a single application.\n# So Go Tend'n'Tinker...\n[### Bonsais\nBrowse some example knowledge bonsais.\n](https://wikibonsai.io/tree)[### Markdown\nTend your markdown notes in VSCode.\n](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=manunamz.vscode-tendr)[### CLI\nTend your markdown notes from the CLI.\n](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tendr-cli/)[### GitHub\nTinker with projects and code.\n](https://github.com/wikibonsai/)[### Consult\nGet help with workflows or tech setup.\n](https://wikibonsai.io/consult)",

    "uri": "https://themetalayer.org/what-is-a-meta-layer",
    "text": "What is a Meta-Layer | Meta-Layer Initiative\n[![Meta-Layer Initiative logo](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=375,fit=crop,q=95/mxB4xDxowEseKBeL/untitled-300-x-85-px--2-mjE75yKbVxFZNJBq.png)](https://themetalayer.org/)\n[![Meta-Layer Initiative logo](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=375,fit=crop,q=95/mxB4xDxowEseKBeL/untitled-300-x-85-px--2-mjE75yKbVxFZNJBq.png)](https://themetalayer.org/)\n# **The Meta-Layer Already Exists. We're Just Naming It.**\nIt’s the decentralized space above the webpage.\nYou’ve seen hints of it in browser extensions, annotations, password managers, and overlay sidebars—now it’s time to build with*purpose*.\n[Explore Meta-Layer Use Cases](https://themetalayer.org/en/en/contribute#contribute)\n### 🌍What is a Meta-Layer?\nYou’ve seen it in tools like:\n* 🖊️Hypothesis –social annotation overlays\n* 🛍️Ground News –media bias indicators\n* 🔐Password managers –interface injection\n* 🤖AI sidebars –real-time summarization and Q&amp;A\nThese are early fragments of a meta-layer—tools that float above webpages, adding value, context, or utility.\nThe difference?\nWe’re building a**composable, open, participant-centered meta-layer**—a system anyone can build on, not a silo or extension.\n![](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=768,h=614,fit=crop/mxB4xDxowEseKBeL/untitled-design-16-dJobqRK9aZt4gzl3.png)\n![](https://assets.zyrosite.com/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,w=375,h=229,fit=crop/mxB4xDxowEseKBeL/untitled-design-16-dJobqRK9aZt4gzl3.png)\n##### *A meta-layer is a shared digital space that exists above the content of a webpage—an interaction and computation environment that responds to what you're looking at, but is not owned by the site itself.*\n### How the Meta-Layer Works\nThe Meta-Layer is:\n* **Triggered by attention**— what you’re focusing on\n* **Built as an overlay**— it doesn’t replace the web, it enhances it\n* **Made of small, meaningful apps**— annotations, tools, badges, tags",
    "title": "What is a Meta-Layer | Meta-Layer Initiative",

    "uri": "https://futuclass.com/blog/educational-vr-games-meta-quest-3/",
    "text": "# Top Educational Games for Meta Quest 3\n\n08/12/2023\n\n[Homeschool](https://futuclass.com/blog/category/3/) [Science Modules](https://futuclass.com/blog/category/20/) [Apps](https://futuclass.com/blog/category/19/)\n\nWhen the main headset of the leading Virtual Reality ecosystem gets an update, everyone pays attention. Meta Quest 3, launched on October 10, improved over its predecessor in almost every way except price. Additionally, Quest 3 was touted to be the first ever mainstream Mixed Reality headset. Let’s look at how each of the improvements affects educational VR experiences, specifically, when using VR in the classroom. This post assumes familiarity with terms such as VR, MR and XR.\n\n#### Mixed Reality looks promising but currently lacks content\n\nMixed Reality, also called “color passthrough”, is the key new technology in Quest 3 for content creators. Compared to Quest 2, the image of the real world shown through the cameras of the headset is much crisper and now has color. Although not quite comparable to human eye vision, it is good enough to enable new use cases such as learning to play real musical instruments (PianoVision, Paradiddle) or figure drawing digital models on real paper using pencil (Gesture VR). Most users would encounter Mixed Reality in the “home scene”, which now makes for a much nicer experience due to color passthrough, improved room detection and joint hand and controller tracking, where the user can be interacting with menus and MR apps in her real-world physical space.\n\n#### Hand tracking is much more useful\n\nA number of software features delivered over the last year have made it more plausible to one day give up controllers altogether for using hands, which is very much a requirement for XR to truly go mainstream. Ability to use hands to interact with menus like with touch screens, simultaneous hand and controller tracking, and overall more responsive and precise hand tracking, especially felt on Quest 3, is a good step towards more inclusive XR devices. Hand tracking feels especially natural when it is combined with Mixed Reality.\n\n#### Automatic Guardian setup\n\nWhen putting on a VR headset, setting up the guardian used to often be the annoying first step (made worse by the fact that Quest 2 often seemed to be forgetting room layouts). With depth sensor added to Quest 3, the headset can now detect objects in the room much more accurately, and can automatically suggest a “play area” based on the perceived layout. This is not necessarily helpful in a classroom setting where with multiple users you may want to draw the borders manually, but for an individual use case it is a nice improvement.",
    "title": "Top Educational Games for Meta Quest 3 - Futuclass",

          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "text": "ODTWÓRZPAUZASTOP\n\nGoogle has introduced a new AI model, Gemini Nano, directly into the Chrome browser, allowing developers to easily utilize advanced AI functions in their web applications. 既然你觉得“小游戏集合”或常规工具还是不够有创意，那我们试着打破“扩展程序只是一个小窗口”的固有思维。

在 2026 年，最酷的前端扩展程序往往是在**改变人与网页的交互方式**，或者将浏览器变成一个**超现实的数字空间**。以下是几个基于纯前端、且极具实验性和趣味性的创意方向：

### 1. 概念：元交互与超现实 (Meta-Interactions)

#### A. "Browser Ghost" (浏览器幽灵) —— 时空胶囊
*   **核心创意**：你在网页上留下的痕迹，会被未来的你（或其他人）发现。
*   **玩法**：你在浏览某个网页（比如 GitHub 某个具体的 issue 或 B 站某个视频）时，可以点击扩展“附体”一段文字或一个涂鸦在那个位置。
*   **有趣点**：当你半年后再次访问这个 URL 时，那个“幽灵”会悄悄浮现，提醒你当时的心情或留下的笔记。
*   **纯前端实现**：将 URL + DOM 路径作为 Key，内容存入 `chrome.storage.local` 或 `sync`。不需要后端，只针对你自己的“数字足迹”。

#### B. "Web Orchestra" (网页交响乐) —— 听觉可视化
*   **核心创意**：每一个网页都有它独特的“声音”。
*   **玩法**：扩展会根据网页的 DOM 结构、颜色分布和链接密度自动生成背景音乐（Generative Music）。
*   **有趣点**：深色模式的网页声音低沉、图片多的网页节奏感强、代码网页清脆响亮。你浏览网页的过程变成了一场实时生成的电子音乐会。
*   **纯前端技术**：使用 **Web Audio API** 和 **Tone.js**，分析 `document.body` 的样式和元素比例。

#### C. "DOM Parkour" (DOM 跑酷) —— 真正的网页交互游戏
*   **核心创意**：你的网页内容就是你的游戏关卡。
*   **玩法**：点击扩展，网页底部会出现一个小人。网页的每一个 `<div>`、`<h1>`、`<p>` 标签都变成了真实的物理平台。
*   **有趣点**：你需要跳过网页上的图片，躲避闪烁的广告，在文字行之间滑行。如果网页布局很乱，游戏难度就越高。
*   **纯前端技术**：利用 **Matter.js** 物理引擎，将 DOM 元素的 `getBoundingClientRect()` 坐标转化为物理世界里的刚体。

### 2. 概念：数据转化与幻觉 (Data Transformation)

#### D. "ASCII Universe" (字符宇宙) —— 复古重构
*   **核心创意**：一键将整个互联网重构成 ASCII 艺术。
*   **玩法**：按下开关，当前网页的所有图片、视频、甚至文字，全部实时转化为动态的 ASCII 字符流。
*   **有趣点**：你可以看着字符组成的 YouTube 视频。这不仅是滤镜，你可以自定义字符集（比如用代码符号重构购物网站）。
*   **纯前端技术**：Canvas 图像处理（像素采样）+ CSS `font-family: monospace`。

#### E. "Digital Garden / WikiBonsai" (数字盆栽) —— 收藏的生命化
*   **核心创意**：你的书签不再是冷冰冰的列表，而是一个成长的森林。
*   **玩法**：每收藏一个网页，侧边栏就会多出一颗种子。如果你经常访问这个网页，树就会长大；如果你很久不看，树会枯萎。
*   **有趣点**：你可以在侧边栏俯瞰你整个知识体系生成的“森林”，点击某棵大树即可跳转回那个网页。
*   **纯前端技术**：SVG 绘图或 Canvas 模拟生长动画 + `chrome.history` / `chrome.bookmarks` API。

### 3. 2026 顶级 Skills：利用 Chrome 内置 AI (Local AI)

#### F. "Alt-Text Dreamer" (视障辅助的浪漫化)
*   **核心创意**：利用 Chrome 2025/2026 内置的 **Gemini Nano (window.ai)**，为网页上没有描述的图片生成“梦幻般的描述”。
*   **玩法**：当鼠标悬停在任何图片上时，本地 AI 会即时生成一段充满诗意的描述。
*   **有趣点**：它不再是生硬的“一张猫的照片”，而是“一只在午后阳光下思考宇宙的虎斑猫”。
*   **纯前端优势**：完全在本地运行，保护隐私，且不消耗任何服务器费用。

---

### 总结建议

如果你追求**绝对的创意**，我个人最推荐 **"DOM Parkour" (跑酷)** 或 **"Web Orchestra" (交响乐)**。这两个方向：
1.  **视觉/听觉冲击力极强**。
2.  **技术挑战适中**（物理引擎 vs 音频合成）。
3.  **极其“解压”**。

**你对“改变网页物理特性”这个方向感兴趣吗？或者你想尝试一下利用浏览器自带的 AI 搞点事情？**

*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "text": "Here's how to make a Y2K website design\n[](https://www.wix.com/studio)\ntop of page\n[FWD](https://www.wix.com/studio/blog)\nOpen search box\nClose Search\nClose Menu\nOpen Menu\nSubscribe\nClose\nSearch\n[Design](https://www.wix.com/studio/blog/category/design)\n# Here&#39;s how to make a Y2K website design\nThe 2000s internet aesthetic is everywhere. Now, bring the look to your next site.\n![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ea1602_50b4b9f6c6c9410ba35cf2890ec8dce8~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_77,h_93,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,blur_2,enc_avif,quality_auto/ea1602_50b4b9f6c6c9410ba35cf2890ec8dce8~mv2.png)\n&#8203;\n![](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/3c2518_30418a08468b491dbbc261e681476ca0~mv2.jpeg)\n{creatorName}\n{6.6.2023}\n{3 min read}\n* ![Writer: Aaron Gelbman]()\nAaron Gelbman\n* Dec 18, 2024\n* 8 min read\nLandlines. iMacs. That screeching sound of dial-up internet that had us waiting to sign online. 2000s tech may not be coming back, but the magic of the Y2K design aesthetic sure is.\nIt’s about time, too. Considering how minimalism has dominated the design landscape since the 2010s, the spirit of the aughts carries with it an energetic air of nostalgia and optimism that we’re ready to embrace. From the resurfacing of Comic Sans, low-fi design and metallics, to major brands reinventing their style by looking back in time—the Y2K aesthetic has re-emerged with even more confidence than the first time around.\nWhat is it about Y2K design that&#x27;s attracting a new generation of trend setters, and how can you create Y2K-inspired web designs? This article will shed light on the hype that is the 2000 aesthetic, diving into the[](https://www.wix.com/studio/blog/design-nostalgia)[design nostalgia](https://www.wix.com/studio/blog/design-nostalgia)that speaks to today’s audience, and showing how you can use this strong-spirited aesthetic in your own[responsive web designs](https://www.wix.com/studio/blog/responsive-web-design).\n**Sign up to build a responsive website**[**on Wix Studio**](https://users.wix.com/signin?studio=true&amp;loginDialogContext=signup&amp;postLogin=https://www.wix.com/intro/studio?ref=studio_login&amp;postSignUp=https://www.wix.com/intro/studio?ref=studio_signup&amp;overrideLocale=en&amp;autoRedirect=true&amp;utm_campaign=https://www.wix.com/studio/blog/y2k-design)**.**\n## What is the Y2K aesthetic?\nPrevalent in popular culture from 1997 to around 2005, the Y2K aesthetic manifested an over-the-top futurism that had a strong impact on the timeline of pop culture and design. It was a visual language that embraced the unknown of a new millennium with an optimistic spirit.\nIn the wake of ’90s angst, the generation that survived the Y2K scare absorbed new technologies quickly and sought the untapped potential of computers and the internet. The dynamic style is a sleek and wild visual representation of futuristic concepts that defined the attitude of this time: metallic colors, icy blues,[](https://www.pocket-lint.com/laptops/news/apple/144413-20-years-of-the-imac-looking-back-at-apple-s-legendary-imac-g3)[translucent hardware](https://www.pocket-lint.com/laptops/news/apple/144413-20-years-of-the-imac-looking-back-at-apple-s-legendary-imac-g3)and[](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2021/11/03/arts/design/neopets.html)[quirky 2D and 3D iconography](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2021/11/03/arts/design/neopets.html).",

    "text": "Learn to build components that work anywhere with [Component Odyssey](https://component-odyssey.com?utm_campaign=a2000_docs_site) ![Build retro user interfaces with modern web technologies](https://a2000-docs.netlify.app/images/cover@2x.png)a2000\n\n# a2000 (a2k)\n\nWelcome to a2000 (or a2k for short).\n\na2000 is a UI library design to capture the feel of the early\nweb using modern web tools and practices.\n\nNote: This is a work in progress and is subjected to change. I\nwelcome any and all feedback!\n\nCheck out the\n[demo](https://a2000.netlify.app/) site for the\nfull a2000 experience. You can also check out the\n[Storybook](https://a2000-storybook.netlify.app/)\nto play around with each component. If you want to use a2000\nin your own projects, you can follow the\n[instructions](https://github.com/andrico1234/a2k).\n\n## Styles\n\na2000 comes with its own default set of styles\n\nYou can add it to your HTML using a CDN, like so:\n\n` `\n\nAdding this stylesheet applies the default base styles,\nvariables, and typefaces.\n\na2000 uses the Pixelated MS Sans Serif typeface.\n\n## Components\n\nTo use the a2000 components in your applications, you'll\nneed to install the a2000 packages using a package manager\nlike npm or yarn.\n\nEach component has a link to the full installation\ninstructions.\n\n### Button\n\nButtons are components that allow your users to perform\nactions. These actions can include opening a modal,\nconfirming an action, confirming a delete request, or\nsubmitting a form.\n\nClick meClick me\n\n[Full demo](https://a2000-storybook.netlify.app/?path=/story/button--default)\n\\|\n[Instructions](https://github.com/andrico1234/a2k/tree/main/packages/button)\n\n### Icons\n\nIcons are pictures that can help a user recognise the\nmeaning of an action/feature quickly. They can also be\nused to improve the visual design of a website.\n\nYou can combine icons with buttons and text to add a\nvisual association to an action. This also increases the\nclick area, which\n[improves the accessibility of the component](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/target-size.html).\n\n[Full demo](https://a2000-storybook.netlify.app/?path=/story/icons--default)\n\\|\n[Instructions](https://github.com/andrico1234/a2k/tree/main/packages/icons)\n\n### Marquee\n\nMarquees are used to insert scrolling text into the web\npage.     "text": "Framer Blog: 15 classic 90s websites + modern sites keeping the aesthetic alive\n[Developers](../../developers/)\n![icon entry point for Site Search](https://framerusercontent.com/images/X8K2iCW5Tob8sQuioDPe6TJEU.png?width=40&amp;height=40)\n###### Search\n[Developers](../../developers/)\n![icon entry point for Site Search](https://framerusercontent.com/images/X8K2iCW5Tob8sQuioDPe6TJEU.png?width=40&amp;height=40)\n###### Search\n[Blog](../)\n/\n[Inspiration](../inspiration)\n## 15classic90swebsites+modernsiteskeepingtheaestheticalive\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/sHz65psCtuokgSMW7nMOfCJ4kxE.png?width=3228&amp;height=2160)\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/sHz65psCtuokgSMW7nMOfCJ4kxE.png?width=3228&amp;height=2160)\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/sHz65psCtuokgSMW7nMOfCJ4kxE.png?width=3228&amp;height=2160)\n[\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/LNJ8cmoS3J8Whw4st8gVgnVW8.jpg?width=1774&amp;height=1645&amp;scale-down-to=22)\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/LNJ8cmoS3J8Whw4st8gVgnVW8.jpg?width=1774&amp;height=1645&amp;scale-down-to=22)\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/LNJ8cmoS3J8Whw4st8gVgnVW8.jpg?width=1774&amp;height=1645&amp;scale-down-to=24)\nJames Pastan\n](https://x.com/jamespastan)\n0 min read\nShare\nShare\nThere’s today’s polished minimalism, and then there’s the internet of the 1990s. Those earliest days of the world wide web used sites as a canvas for raw expression, an era defined by personality-driven chaos that continues to captivate designers and nostalgic users alike.\nThe look and feel of 90s website design was unmistakable. Neon color palettes, static pixelated images, table-based layouts, and custom cursers defined the aesthetic. This style was born from technical constraints like slow dial-up speeds and limited CSS.\nFast-forward to 2025, and modern web design has made huge gains in accessibility and performance. Yet some of the expressiveness has faded. There's an opportunity to bring back that personality-forward visual style with modern quality standards.\n## 15 classic 90s websites\nHere are fifteen classic 90s websites that defined the early world wide web (back when it was still called that, unironically). Many of these old-school websites are preserved in Wayback Machine archives, giving you a peek into the digital past.\n### 1.[Space Jam](https://www.spacejam.com/1996/)\n![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/nrlF7gkqhUe36ft5wXGXyVw2Ges.png)",

    "uri": "https://localghost.dev/blog/building-a-website-like-it-s-1999-in-2022/",
    "text": "Building a website like it&#39;s 1999... in 2022 -\nlocalghost\n[Localghost](https://localghost.dev)choose a theme![](https://localghost.dev/img/garden-icon.png)garden![](https://localghost.dev/img/city-icon.png \"midnight city\")midnight city![](https://localghost.dev/img/sunset-icon.png \"miami sunset\")miami sunsetminimalist![](https://localghost.dev/img/minimalist-icon.png \"minimalist\")2003![](https://localghost.dev/img/2003-icon.png \"2003\")![](https://localghost.dev/img/vaporwave-icon.png \"vaporwave\")vaporwave![](https://localghost.dev/img/netscape-logo.png \"1999\")1999\n# Building a website like it&#39;s 1999... in 2022\nSophie Koonin\n23 October 2022\nTags:\n* [nostalgia](https://localghost.dev/tags/nostalgia/)\n* [fun](https://localghost.dev/tags/fun/)\n* [css](https://localghost.dev/tags/css/)\n* [conferences](https://localghost.dev/tags/conferences/)\n**Edit May 2023:**the Bridgy integration with Twitter no longer works due to Twitter shutting off API access so some functionality won't be working any more!\n*Note: This is a written version of a talk I gave at State of the Browser 2022 in October 2022!*\n**Motion warning**: This page contains quite a few animations, but if you have reduced motion turned on, they won't play.\n## The web used to be weirder\nI'm on a bit of a mission this year to bring back the spirit of the old web. The creativity and flair of the late 90s and early 2000s. Back then, there were no rules –you put whatever you wanted on a webpage, because it was your space to do as you please.\nAnd for a whole generation of internet users, having a website was the cool thing to do. It's just what you did back then. We're talking pre-social media, pre-web 2.0 –the good old fashioned static personal home page.\nSites like Geocities, Angelfire, Tripod and Expage offered free static hosting for all, and the number of personal websites boomed. Some hosts offered drag-and-drop website builders so you didn't even have to learn HTML.\nWe might look back on these websites now and laugh –they look ridiculous compared to the sleek and minimalist sites we're used to nowadays. But I actually think we've gone too far in the other direction, and now so many websites look the same.           <summary>Tool use: **mcp_Graphlit-mcp_webSearch**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

    "uri": "https://www.npmjs.com/package/xp.css/v/0.2.6",
    "text": "## xp.css\n\n0.2.6 • Public • Published 3 years ago\n\n- [Readme](https://www.npmjs.com/www.npmjs.com?activeTab=readme)\n- [Code Beta](https://www.npmjs.com/www.npmjs.com?activeTab=code)\n- [0 Dependencies](https://www.npmjs.com/www.npmjs.com?activeTab=dependencies)\n- [2 Dependents](https://www.npmjs.com/www.npmjs.com?activeTab=dependents)\n- [7 Versions](https://www.npmjs.com/www.npmjs.com?activeTab=versions)\n\n## XP.css\n\nA design system for building faithful recreations of old UIs.\n\nXP.css is an extension of 98.css. A CSS file that takes semantic HTML and makes it look pretty. It does not ship with any JavaScript, so it is compatible with your frontend framework of choice.\n\n### Installation / Usage\n\nThe easiest way to use XP.css is to import it from [unpkg](https://unpkg.com/).\n\n```\n \n \n \n XP.css example \n \n\n \n \n\n \n \n \n\n \n \n \n \n My First Program\n \n \n \n Hello, world! \n \n \n \n \n```\n\nAlternatively, you can grab XP.css from [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/xp.css).\n\n```\nnpm install xp.css\n\nUsage:\n\n// For XP\nimport \"xp.css/dist/XP.css\";\n\n// For 98\nimport \"xp.css/dist/98.css\";\n\n```\n\nHere is an example of [XP.css being used with React](https://codesandbox.io/s/silly-bas-dln9t?file=/src/index.js), and [an example with vanilla JavaScript](https://codesandbox.io/s/vigilant-night-2jkz3?file=/index.html).\n\nRefer to the [documentation page](https://botoxparty.github.io/XP.css/) for specific instructions on this library's components.\n\n### Developing\n\nClone the repo and run `npm install`.\n\nThe core styles are managed in [`gui`](https://github.com/botoxparty/XP.css/tree/main/gui).\n\nTo create your own theme for the GUI you can extend the core styles. See the XP and 98 [`themes`](https://github.com/botoxparty/XP.css/tree/main/themes)\n\nYou can use `npm start` to start a development environment that will watch for file changes and rebuild the files, reloading your browser in the process.\n\nYou can run a build manually with `npm run build`.     Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.

Manifest v2 with `chrome.tabs.insertCSS` to inject CSS with\n`runAt: document_start` in the details of the object when injecting from the background page\n\n[https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/tabs/#method-insertCSS](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/tabs/#method-insertCSS)\n\nThis appears to have been removed with Manifest v3's `chrome.scripting.insertCSS` and there doesn't seem to be a runAt option available anymore for CSS from a background page.\n\n[https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/scripting/#method-insertCSS](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/scripting/#method-insertCSS)\n\nIt now seems to default to `document_idle`\n\nIs there another way of doing it?\nPutting the CSS file in the manifest file isn't really an option as it needs to create the CSS in the background page.\n\nThe new Only the`&quot;matches&quot;`key and either`&quot;js&quot;`or`&quot;css&quot;`are required.\nmanifest.json\n```\n`{\"name\":\"My extension\",...\"content\\_scripts\":[{\"matches\":[\"https://\\*.example.com/\\*\"],\"css\":[\"my-styles.css\"],\"js\":[\"content-script.js\"],\"exclude\\_matches\":[\"\\*://\\*/\\*foo\\*\"],\"include\\_globs\":[\"\\*example.com/???s/\\*\"],\"exclude\\_globs\":[\"\\*bar\\*\"],\"all\\_frames\":false,\"match\\_origin\\_as\\_fallback\":false,\"match\\_about\\_blank\":false,\"run\\_at\":\"document\\_idle\",\"world\":\"ISOLATED\",}],...}`\n```\n## Files\nEach file must contain a relative path to a resource in the extension&#39;s root directory. In Safari and Firefox 102+, this method is also available in Manifest V2.\nTo use this API, you must have the`\"scripting\"`[permission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/permissions)and permission for the target's URL, either explicitly as a[host permission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/permissions#host_permissions)or using the[activeTab permission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/permissions#activetab_permission).\nYou can only inject CSS into pages whose URL can be expressed using a[match pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Match_patterns): meaning its scheme must be one of \"http\", \"https\", or \"file\". This means you can't inject CSS into any of the browser's built-in pages, such as about:debugging, about:addons, or the page that opens when you open a new empty tab.\n**Note:**Firefox resolves URLs in injected CSS files relative to the CSS file rather than the page it's injected into.\nThe inserted CSS can be removed by calling[`scripting.removeCSS()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/scripting/removeCSS).\nThis is an asynchronous function that returns a[`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise).\n## [Syntax](#syntax)\njs\n```\n`await browser.scripting.insertCSS(\ndetails // object\n)`\n```\n### [Parameters](#parameters)\n[`details`](#details)\nAn object describing the CSS to insert and where to insert it. It contains the following properties:\n[`css`Optional](#css)\n`string`. A string containing the CSS to inject. Either`css`or`files`must be specified.\n[`files`Optional](#files)",

[tabs.insertCSS()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/insertCSS)\nTheme\n* OS default\n* Light\n* Dark\nEnglish (US)\nRemember language[](https://github.com/orgs/mdn/discussions/739)Learn more\n* [Deutsch](https://developer.mozilla.org/de/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/insertCSS)\n* [English (US)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/insertCSS)\n* [Français](https://developer.mozilla.org/fr/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/insertCSS)\n* [中文 (简体)](https://developer.mozilla.org/zh-CN/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/insertCSS)\n# tabs.insertCSS()\nInjects CSS into a page.\n**Note:**When using Manifest V3 or higher, use[`scripting.insertCSS()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/scripting/insertCSS)and[`scripting.removeCSS()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/scripting/removeCSS)to insert and remove CSS.\nTo use this API you must have the permission for the page's URL, either explicitly as a[host permission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/permissions#host_permissions), or using the[activeTab permission](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/permissions#activetab_permission).\nYou can only inject CSS into pages whose URL can be expressed using a[match pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Match_patterns): meaning, its scheme must be one of \"http\", \"https\", or \"file\". This means that you can't inject CSS into any of the browser's built-in pages, such as about:debugging, about:addons, or the page that opens when you open a new empty tab.\n**Note:**Firefox resolves URLs in injected CSS files relative to the CSS file itself, rather than to the page it's injected into.\nThe inserted CSS may be removed again by calling[`tabs.removeCSS()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/tabs/removeCSS).\nThis is an asynchronous function that returns a[`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise)(on Firefox only).\n## [Syntax](#syntax)\njs\n```\n`let inserting = browser.tabs.insertCSS(\ntabId, // optional integer\ndetails // object\n)`\n```\n### [Parameters](#parameters)\n[`tabId`Optional](#tabid)\n`integer`. The ID of the tab in which to insert the CSS. Defaults to the active tab of the current window.\n[`details`](#details)\nAn object describing the CSS to insert. It contains the following properties:\n[`allFrames`Optional](#allframes)\n`boolean`. If`true`, the CSS will be injected into all frames of the current page. If it is`false`, CSS is only injected into the top frame. Defaults to`false`.\n[`code`Optional](#code)\n`string`. Code to inject, as a text string.\n[`cssOrigin`Optional](#cssorigin)\n`string`. This can take one of two values: \"user\", to add the CSS as a user stylesheet or \"author\" to add it as an author stylesheet. If this option is omitted, the CSS is added as an author stylesheet.\n* \"user\" enables you to prevent websites from overriding the CSS you insert: see[Cascading order](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Introduction#cascading_order).",

It can read and modify page content using the standard[Web APIs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API). Content script behavior is similar to scripts that are part of a website, such as those loaded using the[`&lt;script&gt;`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script)element). However, content scripts can only access page content when[host permissions for the web page's origin are granted](#permissions).\nContent scripts can access[a small subset of the WebExtension APIs](#webextension_apis), but they can[communicate with background scripts](#communicating_with_background_scripts)using a messaging system and thereby indirectly access the WebExtension APIs.[Background scripts](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Background_scripts)can access all the[WebExtension JavaScript APIs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API)but can't directly access the content of web pages.\n**Note:**Some Web APIs are restricted to[secure contexts](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts), which also applies to content scripts running in these contexts. Except for[`PointerEvent.getCoalescedEvents()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PointerEvent/getCoalescedEvents), which can be called from content scripts in insecure contexts in Firefox.\n## [Loading content scripts](#loading_content_scripts)\nYou can load a content script into a web page:\n1. At install time, into pages that match URL patterns.\n* Using the[`content\\_scripts`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/content_scripts)key in your`manifest.json`, you can ask the browser to load a content script whenever the browser loads a page whose URL[matches a given pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Match_patterns).\n* At runtime, into pages that match URL patterns.\n* Using[`scripting.registerContentScripts()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/scripting/registerContentScripts)or (only in Manifest V2 in Firefox)[`contentScripts`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/contentScripts), you can ask the browser to load a content script whenever the browser loads a page whose URL[matches a given pattern](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/Match_patterns). (This is similar to method 1,*except*that you can add and remove content scripts at runtime.)",

Use the[`&quot;&quot;host\\_permissions&quot;&quot;`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/declare-permissions)key or the[`&quot;activeTab&quot;`](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/activeTab)permission, which grants temporary host permissions. 这个创意太酷了！**“2000年互联网复古化” (The Y2K-ifier)** 是一个极具视觉冲击力和怀旧情怀的方向。

在 2000 年代初（Web 1.0 时代），网页设计的核心特征是：**布局混乱、颜色饱和度高、大量闪烁动画和非常“重”的边框感**。

以下我为你设计的**纯前端实现路线图**，以及一些能让这个插件“灵魂觉醒”的关键创意点：

### 1. 核心视觉特征 (Style Checklist)

要实现这种“穿越感”，我们需要注入一套全局 CSS 来强制覆盖现代网页的样式：

*   **布局重构**：将所有现代的 `Flex` 和 `Grid` 容器强制降级。虽然不能真的把 HTML 改成 `<table>` 布局，但可以用 CSS 给所有 `div` 加上巨大的 **3D 凸起边框 (Beveled Borders)**。
*   **字体降级**：强制全局使用 `Comic Sans MS`, `Times New Roman` 或 `Arial`。文字颜色必须是纯蓝（链接）或纯黑。
*   **经典组件注入**：
    *   **滚动跑马灯 (Marquee)**：给所有标题 `<h1>` - `<h3>` 强制加上 `marquee` 效果。
    *   **背景底纹**：用那种无限平铺的、低分辨率的星空或云朵图片作为全局背景（`background-repeat: repeat`）。
    *   **Under Construction**：在网页右下角自动插入一个“正在建设中”的黄色闪烁 GIF。
*   **交互音效**：点击按钮时播放 Windows 98 的点击声，网页加载时播放拨号上网（Dial-up）的声音。

### 2. 建议技术栈 (2026 Skills Stack)

*   **注入引擎**：使用 **Chrome Manifest V3** 的 `content_scripts` 静态注入基础样式，配合 `chrome.scripting.insertCSS` 动态开关。
*   **CSS 库**：
    *   参考 **[98.css](https://jdan.github.io/98.css/)** 或 **[XP.css](https://botoxparty.github.io/XP.css/)**。这些库已经完美还原了当年的按钮、窗口和滚动条样式。
    *   你可以将这些库的样式通过 `all: unset` 之后的“强力覆盖”模式应用到当前网页。
*   **资源库**：搜集一套 2000 年代常用的 **8-bit 图标** 和 **透明 GIF**。

### 3. 一个更有趣的“进阶”点：动态退化

不仅仅是静态变丑，你可以做一个**“退化进度条”**：
1.  **Level 1 (2010s)**：扁平化消失，阴影和渐变回来。
2.  **Level 2 (2005s)**：按钮变成 3D 凸起，开始出现 Comic Sans 字体。
3.  **Level 3 (2000s)**：满屏的 Marquee 跑马灯，背景变成平铺星空，所有图片变成马赛克。

### 4. 开发起步建议

**第一步：创建一个简单的 `content.css`**
```css
/* 强制所有元素拥有 Windows 98 风格的边框 */
* {
    font-family: "Comic Sans MS", cursive !important;
    border: 2px outset #dfdfdf !important;
    background-color: #c0c0c0 !important;
    color: #000 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
}

/* 所有的链接必须带下划线，且是经典的纯蓝色 */
a {
    color: #0000ee !important;
    text-decoration: underline !important;
}

/* 给图片加上马赛克滤镜 */
img {
    filter: contrast(150%) brightness(1.2) sepia(0.3) blur(0.5px);
    image-rendering: pixelated;
}
```

**第二步：在 `manifest.json` 中配置**
```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "Y2K-ifier",
  "version": "1.0",
  "permissions": ["activeTab", "scripting"],
  "content_scripts": [
    {
      "matches": ["<all_urls>"],
      "css": ["content.css"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**你觉得这个方向如何？我们可以先从实现一个“Windows 98 风格的侧边栏”开始，用来控制网页的“复古程度”。**

The feel like dull everyday pixels.\nIn this tutorial, we&#x27;ll build a whimsical 3D button:\nPush Me\n**Intended audience**\nThis is an intermediate-level tutorial for front-end developers. It&#x27;s focused on HTML/CSS, no JavaScript knowledge required.\nIf you&#x27;re relatively new to CSS transitions, I&#x27;d recommend reading[“An Interactive Guide to CSS Transitions”](https://www.joshwcomeau.com/animation/css-transitions/)first.\n## [Link to this heading](#our-strategy-1)Our strategy\nThere&#x27;s one main trick we&#x27;ll use a couple times in this tutorial to create the*illusion*of a 3D button.\nHere&#x27;s how it works: when the user interacts with our button, we&#x27;ll slide a foreground layer up and down, in front of a stationary background:\nPush Me\nReveal:0\n(Try interacting with the button, after you’ve slid the “Reveal” slider!)\n**Why not use`box-shadow`or`border`?**Those properties are*super*expensive to animate.     "text": "[![CodeinWP](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20728%2090'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://wpshout.com/web-hosting-comparison-chart/?utm_source=ImpressiveWebs&utm_medium=banner&utm_campaign=IW) [![CodeinWP](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20480%20160'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://wpshout.com/web-hosting-comparison-chart/?utm_source=ImpressiveWebs&utm_medium=banner&utm_campaign=IW)\n\nBy [Louis Lazaris](https://www.impressivewebs.com/author/impressive-webs-2/)/ February 25, 2010/ [17 Comments](https://www.impressivewebs.com/cnn-beveled-navigation-buttons-css/#comments)\n\n_Updated: August 7, 2022_\n\n![Beveled Navigation Buttons with Pure CSS](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20184%20184'%3E%3C/svg%3E)When [CNN](http://www.cnn.com/) recently [redesigned their website](http://www.webdesignerdepot.com/2009/11/cnns-new-website-design-deconstructed/), they created a strongly-branded and beautiful header section that includes a navigation bar with beveled buttons. Although CNN’s navigation bar utilizes CSS sprites for highlighted and active buttons, the primary design of the buttons (the beveled effect) is done with pure CSS.\n\nI think this is a commonly-known technique among experienced CSS developers, but many beginning web designers will probably resort to images to create this effect, which is not necessary. So, in this brief tutorial I’ll show you how to create a navigation bar with beveled edges using pure CSS, identical to that on CNN.\n\n[View the demo page](http://www.impressivewebs.com/demo-files/beveled-navigation/beveled-navigation.html) to see exactly what we’ll be creating.\n\nFirst, the markup, which is nothing unusual, just an unordered list:\n\n```\n \n Home \n Video \n NewsPulse \n U.S. \n World \n Politics \n Justice \n Entertainment \n Tech \n Health \n Living \n Travel \n Opinion \n iReport \n Money \n Sports \n \n\n```\n\nThe only thing to note in that code is the class “first”, which will help us round out the effect.\n\nHere’s the CSS for the ` ` element, which has an `id` of `navigation`:\n\n```\n#navigation {\n list-style: none;\n background: #b60002;\n overflow: hidden;\n width: 962px;\n}\n\n```\n\nThe primary navigation element above is styled with a set width, a background color, and a set height. The width is not that important, but it ensures that the element can be centered using `margin: auto`.\n\nNext, we need to style the individual ` ` elements. Here’s the code:\n\n```\n#navigation li {\n float: left;\n border-right: solid 1px #ca0002;\n height: 35px;\n}\n\n```\n\nThe height matches that of the ` ` element, and each ` ` element is given a solid right border, the latter of which constitutes the first part of the beveled effect.\n\nNext are the anchors inside the ` ` elements. Here’s the CSS:\n\n```\n#navigation li a:link, #navigation li a:visited {\n text-decoration: none;\n display: block;\n height: 35px;\n color: #fff;\n line-height: 35px;\n padding: 0 9px 0 9px;\n border-right: solid 1px #990000;\n font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;\n font-size: 12px;\n font-weight: bold;\n}\n\n```\n\nThe important things to note above, again, is the right border setting, which is the second ingredient for getting the beveled effect. Thus, the color of this border is darker than the border on the ` ` element. The rest of the CSS shown above is trivial, making the buttons look similar to those on CNN’s website.\n\n<\n\np>So, although we can’t create a double border on a single element without images, we can get around that by taking advantage of the nested elements that are part of every navigation bar, the anchor and the list item.\n\nNext we give each button a hover state:\n\n```\n#navigation li a:hover {",

I went ahead and gave it a shot.\n\nThese are the steps I took:\n\n- I opened your bitmap in Sketch, my favorite graphical tool for all things web\n- I zoomed in to your bitmap, traced the outline with a rounded rectangle and gave it the correct color\n- I started adding `box-shadow` s, both outside and inset, to replicate the bitmap as close as possible. Note that I only used black and white (with varying alpha values) for the box shadows. This way you can easily change the color of the button by just changing the `background-color`.\n- I also added two extra shapes for the bottom shadow and the top glow, as I did not manage to get this right with just box shadows.     Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.

    "uri": "https://dev.to/debadeepsen/vintage-photo-effect-with-css-16oj",
    "text": "If you, like me, were born in the eighties, you have probably spent some time going through old family photo albums. Back when an album was a physical object that you held in your hands. And even though cameras back in the day lacked the technological prowess of the modern day, the photos were still beautiful in their own way. As a hobbyist photographer myself, I have often used Photoshop and other tools to achieve vintage effects on photos that I took, and simpler tools like Instagram also exist to create similar looks. However, the front-end developer in me got thinking - is there a way to display a photo on the web, like it had been taken in the sixties or seventies? We're in luck, because as it turns out, there is.\n\n## Display only\n\nOne thing that I should be clear about is that this is purely a display-based solution. Which means, the image file isn't manipulated in any way, nor can you save the altered image (other than by taking a screenshot).\n\n## What we'll do\n\nTo make a photo appear \"vintage\", we will be doing the following:\n\n- Add a vignette, aka, a gradient-based darkening around the edges, which was often seen in photos taken by old cameras.\n- Give the picture a yellowish-orangeish tinge, to give the impression of aging.\n- Overlay a subtle film-grainy texture over the image.\n- Blur the image a little, because lenses in the past didn't always have tack-sharp focus.\n- Make some adjustments to brightness, contrast, and saturation.\n\nWe'll be using a few neat things that CSS3 allows us to do, so let's take a look at them now.\n\n## Trick \\#1: Stacking background images.\n\nCSS3 lets you stack multiple background images, on top of one another. This can be used to create really nice-looking overlays (for example, you could make it look like the sun was peeking from behind the clouds, using different image assets for the sun and the clouds). To do so, we use the `background-image` property, and list the image sources separated by commas (the viewing order is start to finish, i.e., images will be placed over the ones succeeding them in the list).\n\nAnother neat thing about CSS is that it treats gradients as images as well. Which means, instead of just chaining multiple images together to form the `background-image` of an element, you could use a mix of gradients and images. We will use this fact to implement various parts of the filter.\n\n#### Vignette\n\nA vignette is literally a radial gradient. We'll use an elliptical shape for it. So the CSS for that would be somewhat like\n\n```\nbackground-image: radial-gradient(ellipse, #0000, #0007);\n\n```\n\nEnter fullscreen modeExit fullscreen mode\n\n#### Tint\n\nWe can use the `linear-gradient` function to add a translucent overlay. Note that, if we specify a gradient with two colors, and set the same values to both, it will behave as a solid block. While we don't need this technique normally, here we actually do, because remember - gradients are valid background images, regular solid colors are not.\n\n```\nbackground-image: linear-gradient(0deg, #9725, #9725);\n\n```\n\nEnter fullscreen modeExit fullscreen mode\n\n> A four digit hex code like `#rgba` is essentially a short way of writing `#rrggbbaa`, where `aa` denotes the alpha channel.",
    "title": "Vintage photo effect with CSS",
    "score": null,
    "__typename": "WebSearchResult"
  },
