    "uri": "https://www.coding-dude.com/wp/css/css-image-effects/",
    "text": "[Skip to content](https://www.coding-dude.com/wp/css/css-image-effects/#content)\n\n![CSS Image Effects](https://www.coding-dude.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/css-image-effects.jpg)\n\nIn this short CSS tutorial I will show you how to create some really cool and easy CSS image effects that you can apply to any online image. The image effects I will show you are the most common photo effects that photographers use when developing a photo.\n\nI’m a photographer myself, so, I like to think that along my [photography journey](https://www.textures4photoshop.com/blog/photographer-journey-beginner-pro-rules-tips/) over the years I’ve learned a thing or two about image effects.\n\nThe CSS image effects I will demonstrate are:\n\n1. Old Paper Overlay\n2. Black and White\n3. Sepia\n4. Warm Colors\n5. Cold Colors\n6. Green Tint\n7. Magenta Tint\n\nThough you can use tools like Photoshop, Lightroom or online tools like MockoFun and their awesome [vintage photo editor](https://www.mockofun.com/tutorials/vintage-photo-editor/) to edit your photos, if you only need to place an image in a web page and apply a filter, here’s how to create cool CSS image effects.\n\n> **NOTE:** One disadvantage of using images with CSS effects is that Google does not see the image with the applied effect. For the purpose of this tutorial, the images below are screenshots of the CSS image effects applied to the original image. They are **NOT the live CSS effect**. If you want to see or play around with the live effects please check this CodePen:\n\nSee the Pen Simple CSS Image Effects by Ion Emil Negoita (@inegoita) on CodePen.\n\n## CSS Image Effects using CSS `filter`\n\nThe `filter` CSS property is a very useful tool when you need to make image adjustments like adjusting the contrast, brightness, saturation etc of images in a web page.\n\nHere’s a list of values that you can use with `filter` in CSS:\n\n- `blur` for adding blur to images\n- `brightness` for making the image brighter or darker\n- `contrast` adjust the contrast of an image\n- `drop-shadow` use as an alternative to `box-shadow`\n- `grayscale` for transforming your image to gray scale\n- `hue-rotate` adjust hue values for your photo\n- `invert` inverts the colors of the image\n- `opacity` alter the transparency of the image\n- `saturate` alter the saturation values of your image\n- `sepia` apply a sepia effect to the image\n\nThese CSS filters take in values (either percent or pixels in the case of `blur` for example). Also, you can apply combinations of these filters to the same image element (or any other HTML element for that matter).\n\nSo, let’s see the CSS `filter` property in action!\n\n## CSS Image Effects: Original Photo\n\nOk, so let’s take this image of an old Volkswagen Beetle I think\n\n![CSS Image Effect](https://www.coding-dude.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/ouDwClz1.jpg)\n\nLet’s apply some cool CSS image effects on it using various values of the `filter` property.\n\nTo create a more vintage effect we’ll also use this [old texture](https://www.photoshopsupply.com/patterns-textures/vintage-paper-textures) from **Vintage Paper Textures** free pack by [PhotoshopSupply](https://www.photoshopsupply.com/). You can also check out this [old paper background](https://www.psd-dude.com/tutorials/resources/beautiful-old-paper-textures.aspx) collection of over 150 different vintage textures.\n\n![Old Texture CSS Image Effect](https://i.imgur.com/4rKVgAQ.png)",
    "title": "7 CSS Image Effects For Making Awesome Vintage Photos",

  },

    "uri": "https://alvaromontoro.com/blog/68020/old-photo-effect-with-css",
    "text": "[Skip to main content](https://alvaromontoro.com/blog/68020/old-photo-effect-with-css#main)\n\nThis article will review how to create an old photo effect on any picture using only CSS. No need for Photoshop or any other image editor. And all in just a few lines of code!\n\nWe will check three different methods that build on top of each other, increasing the old photo effect with each iteration to make it look more realistic and nicer.\n\nFor the examples on this page, we will use a photograph by [Filipp Romanovski](https://unsplash.com/@filipp_roman_photography). You can find it on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/CGKYNN3uuVo), along with many other amazing pictures (by Filipp and many more authors.)\n\n## Using an Image Tag\n\nThe most basic way of creating the old photo effect is directly applying filters to an image in the [` ` tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/img). This method is quick, and the effect will be nice, but the result may be too basic.\n\nLet's start with an image in HTML:\n\n```\n \n\n```\n\nThen we will apply some [filters in CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/filter) and a simple [mask](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/mask):\n\n```\nimg {\n filter: grayscale(1) blur(1px) contrast(1.2) sepia(1);\n -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(#000, #0009);\n}\n\n```\n\nLet's see one by one what each of the filters does:\n\n- `grayscale(1)`: turns the picture into a scale of grays. This will blend some areas together into a similar tone of gray, making the picture lose some detail.\n- `blur(1px)`: applies a Gaussian blur to the image. Enough to combine color regions and make the picture lose more detail.\n- `contrast(1.2)`: sharpens the picture. We can play a little with the value to adjust it to what we want and personalize it for each picture. But beware: too high or too low, and it will look weird.\n- `sepia(1)`: changes the color into an old-photo sepia.\n\nAdditionally, we could add an extra `blur(0.5px)` (it doesn't have to be a round number or higher than 1) to make the photo just a little bit blurry and complete the filter effect. But it's not needed.\n\nThere's one extra line for `-webkit-mask`. Old photos seem more focused in the center, but then they degrade, losing color and getting a bit blurry toward the edges. We can achieve that by applying a mask in CSS. [Unfortunately, `mask` is not supported by all browsers](https://caniuse.com/?search=mask)... luckily for us, the vendor prefix is! So we can apply the same effect using `-webkit-mask`.",
    "title": "Old Photo Effect with CSS",
    "score": null,
    "__typename": "WebSearchResult"

    "text": "[Skip to content](https://expertbeacon.com/expertbeacon.com#main)\n\nGrainy, glitchy backgrounds are becoming increasingly popular in modern web design. When used deliberately, these retro, degraded effects create intrigue and depth to complement sleek interfaces.\n\nIn this comprehensive guide, we‘ll explore several methods for generating grainy backgrounds with CSS and SVG filters.\n\n**We‘ll cover:**\n\n- The appeal of the grainy aesthetic\n- Using PNG images for grain overlays\n- Leveraging SVG noise textures\n- Coding noise filters directly into CSS\n- Performance data on image formats\n- More experiments for creating vintage effects\n\nWhether you‘re an aspiring or seasoned developer, this deep dive will level up your creative background skills!\n\n## The Return of Grunge: Why Grainy Backgrounds Work\n\nBefore we get technical, it‘s worth understanding _why_ grainy backgrounds have become popular again.\n\nTrends tend to echo broader cultural shifts. And after years of flat, minimalist design, interfaces are infusing more texture and grit to better resonate with users.\n\nThis grungy aesthetic connects us to familiar textures in the physical world, much like the return of [skeuomorphic design](https://www.invisionapp.com/inside-design/skeuomorphism-ux/) and hand-drawn illustration styles.\n\nAnd visually, the noise and artifacts provide depth and contrast to hero sections and image headers:\n\nSo while glitches may seem like a regression in interface quality, they tap into deeper emotional associations. Users find imperfection and nostalgia highly relatable.\n\nNow let‘s break down some techniques to recreate these effects!\n\n## Method 1: Overlaying PNG Noise Textures\n\nThe most straightforward approach is overlaying transparent PNG images containing grain, grunge, and noise. By compositing the texture over a colored background, we achieve the grainy effect.\n\nFor example, here‘s how the developers at Arc add vintage flair to their homepage hero:\n\n```\n.hero {\n background: var(--color-primary);\n background-image: url(noise.png);\n}\n```\n\n- `--color-primary` provides the base background color\n- `noise.png` overlays the grainy texture\n\n- `noise.png` is a transparent noise texture at a low opacity:\n\nAdvantages of using PNGs:\n\n- Simple implementation\n- Wide browser support\n\nDisadvantages:\n\n- Can increase page weight",

    "text": "![Arrow left](https://devot.team/blog/w_64/f_svg/q_auto/v1//images/arrow_pq6n4y?_a=BAVAZGDW0)Back to blogs\n\n# How to Optimize Images for Web Without Losing Quality?\n\nMax L.7 min readDec 16, 2022 [Technology](https://devot.team/blog?category=technology)\n\nMax L.7 min read\n\nLink copied!\n\nContents:\n\nPraise originality\n\nSEO friendliness\n\nPerformance & optimization\n\nLazy loading\n\nVisual representation\n\nImplementation examples\n\nNew image formats\n\nConclusion\n\nHow often do you come across sites with little to no imagery? Right - barely ever. Such occasions happen, but broadly speaking, websites usually contain\nsome forms of visual representations to provide better context or clarification. After all, images are the primary form of visual identity online. They\nbreak up the monotony of the text and give insight into what the story being told is all about. Images are powerful means of communication, and if used\nproperly, they can yield purpose to your site too.\n\nBut before blindly adding relevant images or graphics to your site, consider reading the rest of this blog to understand better why and how you should\nhandle visuals to maximize value and get the point across better.\n\n## Praise originality\n\nUse original images. Make people feel like they're visiting a place they have not already seen beforehand. Make their stay a welcome and remarkable\nexperience. **Showing originality through your visuals greatly improves the experience one has with the brand or company**. The images here\nto look out for are either of your workplace, company, staff members, or some products.\n\n## SEO friendliness\n\nSEO (Search Engine Optimization) is the term that either breaks a website or makes it shine. We're all familiar with it, and knowing that, we shall not\nallow our website to load slowly. If it does, readers may lose patience and leave the site quickly. On the other hand, if your website is SEO-friendly,\nGoogle and other search engines can effectively index every page on your website. That way, the site has a higher reach and a higher likelihood of being\nshown as a result of the end user's search query.\n\n## Performance & optimization\n\nImages take up memory and storage. The more you have, the harder they are to handle. For that reason alone, optimization is the top priority. Slowing the\npage down causes stutters and, in turn, negatively affects the end-user experience. We don't want that. Higher-resolution images take up more storage due\nto effectively having more content within themselves.\n\nSo to improve the performance and optimization of images, web developers mostly use these three methods: **caching**,\n**compressing**, and **resizing**. With the caching method, images are stored in the browser's cache or proxy server so that they\ncan be accessed easily. This method reduces application requests and the page's download size. The compression method makes images smaller by reducing the\nnumber of bits. **Finally, it would help if you considered compressing images to prevent overload and improve the experience of using the**\n**page**. In case you can't compress your images, you can resize them. But remember that you must balance the image size and resolution.\n\nAs for image optimization, it is possible in two ways - **manual** and **automatic**. Manual image optimization is done using\nvarious online image compressors that deliver high-quality compressed files. The most popular ones are:\n\n- [Optimizilla](https://imagecompressor.com/)\n\n- [TinyPNG](https://tinypng.com/)\n\n- [JPEG Optimizer](https://jpeg-optimizer.com/)",

    "uri": "https://leanrada.com/notes/css-only-lqip/",
    "text": "Here’s a CSS technique that produces blurry image placeholders (LQIPs) without cluttering up your markup — _Only a single custom property needed!_\n\nGranted, it’s a _very blurry_ placeholder especially in contrast to other leading solutions. But the point is that it’s minimal and non-invasive! No need for wrapper elements or attributes with long strings of data, or JavaScript at all.\n\n## Example images\n\n## Survey of LQIP approaches\n\nThere have been many different techniques to implement LQIPs (low quality image placeholders), such as a very low\nresolution WebP or JPEG ( [beheaded JPEGs](https://engineering.fb.com/2015/08/06/android/the-technology-behind-preview-photos/) even), optimised SVG shape placements ( [SQIP](https://github.com/axe312ger/sqip)), and directly applying a discrete cosine\ntransform ( [BlurHash](https://blurha.sh/)). Don’t forget good old progressive JPEGs and interlaced\nPNGs!\n\nCanva and Pinterest use solid colour placeholders.\n\nAt the other end of the spectrum, we have low tech solutions such as a simple solid fill of the image’s average colour.\n\nPure inline CSS solutions have the advantage rendering immediately — even a `background-image: url(…a data URL)` would be fine!\n\n[Gradify](https://github.com/fraser-hemp/gradify) generates linear-gradients\nthat very roughly approximate the full image.\n\nThe big disadvantage of pure CSS approaches is that you typically litter your markup with lengthy inline styles or obnoxious data URLs. My handcoded site with no build step would be extra incompatible with this approach!\n\n**[BlurHash](https://blurha.sh/)** is a solution that minimises markup by compressing image\ndata into a\n**short base-83 string**, but decoding and rendering that data requires additional JS…\n\nBlurHash example\n\nIs it possible to decode a blur hash in CSS instead?\n\n## Decoding in pure CSS\n\nUnlike BlurHash, we can’t use a string encoding because there are very few if any string manipulation\nfunctions in CSS (2025), so strings are out.\n\nIn the end, I came up with my own hash / encoding, and the **integer** type was the best vessel for it.\n\nThe usual way to encode stuff in a single integer is by [**bit packing**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bit_manipulation), where you pack multiple numbers in an integer as bits. Amazingly, we can unpack them in pure CSS!",
    "title": "Minimal CSS-only blurry image placeholders",

  },

    "uri": "https://mangohost.net/blog/guide-how-to-style-images-with-css/",
    "text": "Styling images with CSS is one of those fundamental skills that separates the pros from the beginners when it comes to web development. Whether you’re building a responsive web app that needs to handle images gracefully across different devices, or you’re setting up a server-side rendered application that needs to deliver optimized visual content, understanding how to properly manipulate images with CSS will save you countless hours and prevent those frustrating layout breaks that make users bounce. In this guide, we’ll dive deep into CSS image styling techniques, from basic responsive setups to advanced filter effects and performance optimizations that actually matter in production environments. \n How CSS Image Styling Works \n CSS image styling operates on several levels of the rendering pipeline. When a browser encounters an &lt;img&gt; element or a background image, it first calculates the intrinsic dimensions, then applies any CSS rules that modify sizing, positioning, or visual effects. The key difference between inline images and background images is how they interact with the document flow and how they handle responsiveness. \n Inline images ( &lt;img&gt; tags) are replaced elements that maintain their aspect ratio by default and participate in the normal document flow. Background images, on the other hand, are purely decorative and don’t affect layout unless you’re using them in combination with padding or specific sizing techniques. \n The CSS box model applies to images just like any other element, but there are some gotchas. The width and height properties directly control the display size, while object-fit and object-position determine how the actual image content fits within those bounds. \n Step-by-Step Implementation Guide \n Let’s start with the basics and work our way up to more complex scenarios. First, here’s how to make images responsive by default: \n /* Basic responsive image setup */\nimg {\n max-width: 100%;\n height: auto;\n display: block;\n}\n/* For better performance and loading experience */\nimg {\n max-width: 100%;\n height: auto;\n display: block;\n loading: lazy; /* HTML attribute, but crucial for performance */\n}\n \n Now let’s implement more advanced sizing techniques using object-fit, which is incredibly useful when you need consistent dimensions: \n /* Fixed aspect ratio containers */\n.image-container {\n width: 300px;\n height: 200px;\n overflow: hidden;\n}\n.image-container img {\n width: 100%;\n height: 100%;\n object-fit: cover; /* Crops to fill, maintains aspect ratio */\n object-position: center;\n}\n/* Alternative approaches for different use cases */\n.contain-image {\n object-fit: contain; /* Shows entire image, may have letterboxing */\n}\n.fill-image {\n object-fit: fill; /* Stretches to fill, may distort */\n}\n.scale-down-image {\n object-fit: scale-down; /* Behaves like contain or none, whichever is smaller */\n}\n \n For background images, the implementation is different but equally powerful: \n /* Background image responsive setup */\n.hero-section {\n background-image: url('hero-image.jpg');\n background-size: cover;\n background-position: center;\n background-repeat: no-repeat;\n min-height: 400px;\n width: 100%;\n}\n/* High-DPI display optimization */\n.hero-section {\n background-image: url('hero-image.jpg');\n}\n@media (-webkit-min-device-pixel-ratio: 2), (min-resolution: 192dpi) {\n .hero-section {\n background-image: url('hero-image@2x.jpg');\n }\n}\n \n Here’s how to implement a flexible grid system for image galleries: \n /* CSS Grid approach for image galleries */\n.image-grid {\n display: grid;\n grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr));\n gap: 20px;\n padding: 20px;\n}\n.image-grid img {\n width: 100%;\n height: 250px;\n object-fit: cover;\n border-radius: 8px;\n transition: transform 0.3s ease;\n}\n.image-grid img:hover {\n transform: scale(1.05);\n}\n/* Flexbox alternative */\n.image-flex {\n display: flex;\n flex-wrap: wrap;\n gap: 20px;\n}\n.image-flex .image-item {",
    "title": "Guide: How to Style Images with CSS - MangoHost",

*Called tool*: Graphlit-mcp - webSearch: Performs web or podcast search based on search query. Can search for web pages or anything about podcasts (i.e. episodes, topics, guest appearances). 
    Format the search query as what would be entered into a Google search. You can use site filtering in the search query, like 'site:twitter.com'.    
    Accepts search query as string, and optional search service type.    
    Prefer calling this tool over using 'curl' directly for any web search.
    Use 'PODSCAN' search service type to search podcasts.
    Does *not* ingest pages or podcast episodes into Graphlit knowledge base.  
    When searching podcasts, *don't* include the term 'podcast' or 'episode' in the search query - that would be redundant.
    Search service types: Tavily (web pages), Exa (web pages), ExaCode (code & docs) and Podscan (podcasts). Defaults to Exa.
    Returns URL, title and relevant Markdown text from resulting web pages or podcast episode descriptions.

  * query: CSS to style all headers and text in retro 2000s web style without changing size unchanged

    "text": "[Learn](https://1stwebdesigner.com/category/learn)[Web Design](https://1stwebdesigner.com/category/webdesign)[#CSS](https://1stwebdesigner.com/tag/css)[#Guides](https://1stwebdesigner.com/tag/guides)[#web design](https://1stwebdesigner.com/tag/web-design)\n\n# Retro CSS Text Effect: A Step-by-Step Tutorial\n\nJuly 4, 2023   \\|   [1WD Crew](https://1stwebdesigner.com/author/code-tips-and-news/)\n\nCSS offers an array of tools that, when used correctly, can improve the visual experience on your website. In this tutorial, we’ll explore a straightforward way to design a retro text effect with pure CSS. The approach, while not overly complex, yields a visually appealing result and serves as a foundation for further customization.\n\n## The HTML Setup\n\nWe’ll begin with our markup, containing the text we’ll be styling – “ **1stWebDesigner**“.\n\n```\n 1stWebDesigner \n\n```\n\nThe div class `.retro-text` will be the hook for our CSS styling.\n\n## Designing the Retro Style with CSS\n\nNext, let’s move on to our CSS file to create the retro text effect.\n\n```\n@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lobster+Two:wght@700&display=swap');\n\nbody {\n background: #6868AC; /* Retro background color */\n}\n\n.retro-text {\n font-family: 'Lobster Two', serif; /* Stylish, retro font */\n font-size: 10vw; /* Responsive font size */\n position: relative; /* Enables use of z-index */\n color: #F9f1cc; /* Primary color of the text */\n text-shadow: -2px 2px 0 #FFB650, /* Orange shadow */\n -4px 4px 0 #FF80BF, /* Pink shadow */\n -6px 6px 0 #6868AC; /* Dark blue shadow */\n transform: skewX(-10deg); /* Skew the text on the X-axis */\n transition: all 0.5s ease; /* Smooth transition for hover effects */\n z-index: 2; /* Ensures text is layered above any potential background or border */\n}\n\n.retro-text:hover {\n color: #FFFFFF; /* Brighter color on hover */\n font-size: 15vw; /* Slightly larger text on hover */\n text-shadow: -2px 2px 0 #FFC162, /* Brighter orange shadow on hover */\n -4px 4px 0 #FF92D0, /* Brighter pink shadow on hover */\n -6px 6px 0 #8888D3; /* Brighter blue shadow on hover */\n}\n\n```\n\nTo explain our CSS setup:\n\n- `font-family: 'Lobster Two', serif;`: We’re using Lobster Two, a stylish retro font.\n- `font-size: 10vw;`: Sets a responsive font size that adapts to the viewport width.\n- `position: relative;`: The relative positioning is necessary for the use of the z-index property.\n- `color: #F9f1cc;`: This determines the primary color of the text. Here, we’re using #F9f1cc, a light cream color.\n- `text-shadow: -2px 2px 0 #FFB650, -4px 4px 0 #FF80BF, -6px 6px 0 #6868AC;`: Three layers of text-shadow (orange, pink, and dark blue) are added, creating a 3D effect that enhances the retro feel.\n- `transform: skewX(-10deg);`: The text is skewed on the X-axis to add a dynamic touch.\n- `transition: all 0.5s ease;`: Smooth transition for hover effects.",

    "text": "# Create a retro text effect with CSS\n\n## April 13, 2021\n\nIn this article, we're going to create an 80's style text effect with CSS. The effect uses multiple `text-shadow`, `background-clip`, `filter`, linear gradients and `-webkit-text-stroke` to achieve a cool metallic effect.\n\nBefore we dive into the actual CSS you probably want to see the end result.\n\nLet's start by defining our HTML markup that we will be using.\n\n```\n\n \n \n \n \n \n \n Retro effect with CSS \n \n \n \n \n Retro \n effect \n \n With CSS \n \n \n \n```\n\nThe HTML markup has a container `div` element and two header elements. The `h1` element has two `span` elements that have the text _Retro_ and _effect_. The text is split into to `span` elements so we can apply the effect to both of them individually.\n\nThe `container`, `title` and `subtitle` classes define mostly positioning rules so we won't be covering them. You can find the full CSS code in the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/juhanakristian/retro-effect-with-css).\n\nThe `span` elements have two classes that we will use to define our effect. Let's create the metallic fill for the text by adding a `metal` CSS class.\n\nAdd the following code inside the `head` tags in the HTML.\n\n```\n\n \n.metal{\nbackground:linear-gradient(\nhsl(239,50%,30%)15%,\nhsl(239,50%,40%)25%,\nhsl(200,60%,50%)35%,\nhsl(100,70%,80%)45%,\nhsl(60,100%,98%)50%,\nhsl(240,0%,0%)52%,\nhsl(240,10%,10%)60%,\nhsl(240,50%,30%)70%,\nhsl(220,70%,60%)80%,\nhsl(212,92%,76%)85%\n);\n}\n \n```\n\nThis will define a background for our text consisting of a linear gradient with ten colors. The output will look like this.\n\nThe gradient goes from darker blue to a greenish almost white, then there's a hard transition to black and a gradient to ligh blue. This creates an effect of metallic reflection and shine.\n\nBut how do we use the gradient as fill for the text and not a background? This can be done using the `background-clip` rule. Let's add the following rules to our `.metal` class.\n\n```\n\n.metal{\n/* ... */\ncolor: transparent;\nbackground-clip: text;\n-webkit-background-clip: text;\n}\n```\n\n`background-clip: text` creates a clipping mask from the text and uses it as a mask when rendering the background. Only the area of the clipping mask is rendered. The text itself is also rendered, so we need to add `color: transparent` to prevent it from covering the background. For this to work on WebKit-based browsers we need to add `-webkit-background-clip: text`.\n\nNext, as a polish 😜, we'll add a border to the text. If we would just add `border: ...` we would get a box-shaped border for the whole element, which is not what we want. 🤔\n\nLuckily, there's a non-standard CSS rule `-webkit-text-stroke` which is [supported by all the major browsers except IE](https://caniuse.com/text-stroke). Firefox and Edge support the `webkit` prefix version and don't have their own prefix.",

这个“手术级”复古化的想法非常细腻！不改变布局和大小，意味着我们只对元素的“皮肤”进行重塑，这不仅能保持现代网页的可用性，还能产生一种奇妙的“平行时空”错觉。

以下是针对**按钮、文字、标题、图片**四个核心元素的复古化方案，这些 CSS 属性只会改变视觉样式，不会干扰 `flex`、`grid` 或原本的尺寸。

### 1. 按钮 (Buttons)：经典 3D 凸起效果
2000 年代的按钮必须有那种沉重的、通过边框实现的 3D 感。

```css
/* 针对所有按钮和类按钮元素 */
button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], .btn {
    background-color: #c0c0c0 !important; /* 经典的灰白色 */
    border-top: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
    border-left: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
    border-bottom: 2px solid #808080 !important;
    border-right: 2px solid #808080 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important; /* 强制直角 */
    padding: 2px 10px !important;
    color: #000000 !important;
    box-shadow: none !important;
    text-shadow: none !important;
    cursor: pointer !important;
}

/* 模拟按下效果 */
button:active, .btn:active {
    border-top: 2px solid #808080 !important;
    border-left: 2px solid #808080 !important;
    border-bottom: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
    border-right: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
}
```

### 2. 文字与标题 (Typography)：字体的穿越
文字是复古感的核心。我们要锁定当时的常用字体，并对链接做特殊处理。

```css
/* 全局基础文字 */
body, p, span, li, td {
    font-family: Arial, "MS Sans Serif", sans-serif !important;
    font-weight: normal !important;
}

/* 标题样式：带点阴影或特殊的复古色 */
h1, h2, h3 {
    font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif !important;
    color: #000080 !important; /* 经典深蓝色 */
    text-transform: none !important;
    letter-spacing: normal !important;
}

/* 链接：必须带下划线，且是那种纯正的蓝色 */
a {
    color: #0000ee !important;
    text-decoration: underline !important;
}
a:visited {
    color: #551a8b !important; /* 经典的已访问紫色 */
}
```

### 3. 图片 (Images)：低保真滤镜
通过 CSS 滤镜，让现代的高清大图看起来像 2000 年那种经过高倍率压缩的 JPEG。

```css
img {
    /* 增加对比度、稍微偏黄、边缘模糊 */
    filter: contrast(110%) sepia(20%) brightness(105%) !important;
    /* 让缩放时产生像素感而非平滑模糊 */
    image-rendering: pixelated !important;
    /* 给图片加一个灰色的细边框 */
    border: 1px solid #808080 !important;
}
```

### 4. 复古细节：系统风格的滚动条
这是点睛之笔，让整个浏览器窗口看起来都像 Windows 2000。

```css
::-webkit-scrollbar {
    width: 16px !important;
    height: 16px !important;
}
::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
    background: #dfdfdf url('data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAIAAAACCAYAAABytg0kAAAAFElEQVQImWNkYGBoYGBgYmBgYAAAAAYAAfL0V74AAAAASUVORK5CYII=') repeat !important; /* 模拟那种网格底纹 */
}
::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
    background-color: #c0c0c0 !important;
    border: 2px outset #ffffff !important;
}
```

### 技术实现 Skills & Steps

1.  **静态注入**：在 `manifest.json` 的 `content_scripts` 中引入这个 `retro.css`。
2.  **选择性排除**：现代网页有很多图标字体（如 FontAwesome），你可以通过 `:not([class*="icon"])` 来避免把图标也变丑了。
3.  **开关控制**：在 Popup 页面做一个“复古模式”开关，通过 `chrome.scripting.insertCSS` 和 `removeCSS` 实现实时切换。

**这个方案最大的魅力在于：它只是给现代互联网穿上了一件 20 年前的旧西装，内容没变，但气质全变了。你觉得这样的视觉改造符合你的预期吗？**

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,34 @@
- 
+ # Requirements - Y2K-ifier
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ The **Y2K-ifier** is a Google Chrome extension designed to surgically transform the visual style of modern web pages into a "2000s retro" aesthetic. The primary goal is to provide a nostalgic user experience without compromising the usability or layout of the original websites.
+ 
+ ## User Stories
+ | ID | User Story | Acceptance Criteria |
+ |----|------------|---------------------|
+ | US.1 | **Toggle Retro Style** | The user must be able to turn the retro transformation on or off via a popup interface. |
+ | US.2 | **Surgical Visual Transformation** | Modern UI elements (buttons, headers, text, images) should look like they are from the year 2000. |
+ | US.3 | **Layout Preservation** | The transformation must NOT change the size, position, or layout of any elements on the page. |
+ | US.4 | **Persistence** | The toggle state (On/Off) must be remembered across different tabs and browser restarts. |
+ | US.5 | **Cross-Site Compatibility** | The extension should function reliably on a wide variety of modern web structures. |
+ 
+ ## Functional Requirements
+ - **FR.1: CSS Injection**: The extension must inject a specific "retro stylesheet" into the active tab.
+ - **FR.2: Surgical Targeting**:
+     - **Buttons**: Apply 3D beveled borders and grey background (&#96;#c0c0c0&#96;).
+     - **Typography**: Force serif fonts for headers (Times New Roman) and sans-serif for body text (Arial/MS Sans Serif). Force blue underlined links.
+     - **Images**: Apply low-fidelity filters (pixelated rendering, slight sepia/contrast adjustment).
+     - **Scrollbars**: Skin the scrollbars to match the classic Windows 2000 look.
+ - **FR.3: Toggle Logic**: A persistent state manager using &#96;chrome.storage.local&#96;.
+ - **FR.4: UI Interface**: A simple popup with a toggle switch.
+ 
+ ## Non-Functional Requirements
+ - **NFR.1: Performance**: CSS injection should be near-instantaneous and not cause significant layout shift.
+ - **NFR.2: Privacy**: Purely frontend, no data collection or external API calls.
+ - **NFR.3: Reliability**: The injected CSS must use &#96;!important&#96; to override modern site styles effectively but cautiously.
+ 
+ ## EARS Criteria Compliance
+ - **Event-driven**: *When* the user toggles the switch, *then* the CSS should be applied or removed.
+ - **Ubiquitous**: *Where* the extension is active, *the system shall* style all buttons with beveled borders.
+ - **Unwanted Behavior**: *If* a site uses complex icon fonts, *the system shall* attempt to exclude them from font-family overrides to maintain usability.
+ 
```

```diff
- # Requirements - Y2K-ifier
+ # 需求文档 - Y2K-ifier (2000年代复古化插件)
  
- ## Overview
- The **Y2K-ifier** is a Google Chrome extension designed to surgically transform the visual style of modern web pages into a "2000s retro" aesthetic. The primary goal is to provide a nostalgic user experience without compromising the usability or layout of the original websites.
+ ## 概述
+ **Y2K-ifier** 是一款谷歌浏览器扩展插件，旨在通过“手术级”的视觉重塑，将现代网页的风格转化为 2000 年代的复古审美。其核心目标是在不破坏原始网站可用性或布局的前提下，为用户提供纯粹的怀旧体验。
  
- ## User Stories
- | ID | User Story | Acceptance Criteria |
+ ## 用户故事
+ | ID | 用户故事 | 验收标准 |
  |----|------------|---------------------|
- | US.1 | **Toggle Retro Style** | The user must be able to turn the retro transformation on or off via a popup interface. |
- | US.2 | **Surgical Visual Transformation** | Modern UI elements (buttons, headers, text, images) should look like they are from the year 2000. |
- | US.3 | **Layout Preservation** | The transformation must NOT change the size, position, or layout of any elements on the page. |
- | US.4 | **Persistence** | The toggle state (On/Off) must be remembered across different tabs and browser restarts. |
- | US.5 | **Cross-Site Compatibility** | The extension should function reliably on a wide variety of modern web structures. |
+ | US.1 | **切换复古风格** | 用户必须能够通过插件弹出界面（Popup）开启或关闭复古转换。 |
+ | US.2 | **手术级视觉重塑** | 现代 UI 元素（按钮、标题、文本、图片）应看起来像来自 2000 年。 |
+ | US.3 | **布局保护** | 转换过程中不得改变页面上任何元素的大小、位置或原始布局。 |
+ | US.4 | **状态持久化** | 开启/关闭状态必须在不同标签页和浏览器重启后保持。 |
+ | US.5 | **跨站兼容性** | 插件应能在各种现代网页结构上稳定运行。 |
  
- ## Functional Requirements
- - **FR.1: CSS Injection**: The extension must inject a specific "retro stylesheet" into the active tab.
- - **FR.2: Surgical Targeting**:
-     - **Buttons**: Apply 3D beveled borders and grey background (&#96;#c0c0c0&#96;).
-     - **Typography**: Force serif fonts for headers (Times New Roman) and sans-serif for body text (Arial/MS Sans Serif). Force blue underlined links.
-     - **Images**: Apply low-fidelity filters (pixelated rendering, slight sepia/contrast adjustment).
-     - **Scrollbars**: Skin the scrollbars to match the classic Windows 2000 look.
- - **FR.3: Toggle Logic**: A persistent state manager using &#96;chrome.storage.local&#96;.
- - **FR.4: UI Interface**: A simple popup with a toggle switch.
+ ## 功能需求
+ - **FR.1: CSS 注入**：插件必须将特定的“复古样式表”注入到当前活动标签页中。
+ - **FR.2: 手术级目标定位**：
+     - **按钮 (Buttons)**：应用 3D 凸起边框和灰色背景 (&#96;#c0c0c0&#96;)。
+     - **排版 (Typography)**：标题强制使用衬线字体 (Times New Roman)，正文使用无衬线字体 (Arial/MS Sans Serif)。强制链接显示蓝色及下划线。
+     - **图片 (Images)**：应用低保真滤镜（像素化渲染、轻微的褐色/对比度调节）。
+     - **滚动条 (Scrollbars)**：重塑滚动条外观，使其匹配经典的 Windows 2000 风格。
+ - **FR.3: 开关逻辑**：使用 &#96;chrome.storage.local&#96; 管理持久化的开关状态。
+ - **FR.4: 用户界面**：提供一个带有开关按钮的简洁弹出界面。
  
- ## Non-Functional Requirements
- - **NFR.1: Performance**: CSS injection should be near-instantaneous and not cause significant layout shift.
- - **NFR.2: Privacy**: Purely frontend, no data collection or external API calls.
- - **NFR.3: Reliability**: The injected CSS must use &#96;!important&#96; to override modern site styles effectively but cautiously.
- 
- ## EARS Criteria Compliance
- - **Event-driven**: *When* the user toggles the switch, *then* the CSS should be applied or removed.
- - **Ubiquitous**: *Where* the extension is active, *the system shall* style all buttons with beveled borders.
- - **Unwanted Behavior**: *If* a site uses complex icon fonts, *the system shall* attempt to exclude them from font-family overrides to maintain usability.
+ ## 非功能需求
+ - **NFR.1: 性能**：CSS 注入应接近即时，且不引起明显的布局偏移（Layout Shift）。
+ - **NFR.2: 隐私**：纯前端开发，不收集任何数据，不调用外部 API。
+ - **NFR.3: 可靠性**：注入的 CSS 必须谨慎使用 &#96;!important&#96;，以有效但克制地覆盖现代网站样式。
+ 
+ ## EARS 标准合规性
+ - **事件驱动 (Event-driven)**：*当* 用户切换开关时，*系统应* 应用或移除复古 CSS。
+ - **普遍存在 (Ubiquitous)**：*在* 插件激活的情况下，*系统应* 为所有按钮添加 3D 凸起边框。
+ - **异常行为 (Unwanted Behavior)**：*如果* 网站使用了复杂的图标字体，*系统应* 尝试排除这些元素的字体族覆盖，以保持图标的可用性。
  
```

```diff
- 
+ # 技术设计文档 - Y2K-ifier
+ 
+ ## 概述
+ **Y2K-ifier** 是一个基于 Chrome Extension Manifest V3 的纯前端插件。它通过注入专门设计的 CSS 样式表，在不改变现代网页结构的情况下，实现视觉上的“2000年代化”。该设计采用模块化结构，将样式定义、注入逻辑和用户界面分离。
+ 
+ ## 指导文档对齐
+ 由于本项目目前处于初期阶段，尚未建立正式的 &#96;tech.md&#96; 或 &#96;structure.md&#96;，本项目将遵循标准的 Chrome 扩展开发模式。
+ 
+ ## 代码复用分析
+ 目前仓库为空，没有现成的代码可供复用。我们将从零开始构建。
+ 
+ ## 架构设计
+ 本插件将由三个核心模块组成：
+ 1.  **Popup (用户界面)**：提供一个简单的 HTML/CSS 开关，允许用户控制复古模式。
+ 2.  **Service Worker (后台逻辑)**：监听浏览器事件（如标签页更新），并根据存储的状态管理 CSS 的注入。
+ 3.  **Content Scripts (内容注入)**：负责实际将 &#96;retro.css&#96; 注入到目标网页。
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid
+ graph TD
+     A[Popup UI] -- 发送状态变更 --&gt; B[chrome.storage.local]
+     B -- 状态持久化 --&gt; C[Service Worker]
+     C -- 监听 URL 变更/存储变更 --&gt; D[Scripting API]
+     D -- 注入/移除 --&gt; E[retro.css]
+     E -- 作用于 --&gt; F[Active Webpage]
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## 组件与接口
+ 
+ ### 1. Popup 模块
+ -   **目的**：提供用户控制开关。
+ -   **接口**：
+     -   &#96;onToggleChange(state)&#96;：更新 &#96;chrome.storage.local&#96; 中的 &#96;isEnabled&#96; 标志。
+ -   **依赖**：&#96;chrome.storage&#96; API。
+ 
+ ### 2. Service Worker (background.js)
+ -   **目的**：全局状态监听与自动注入管理。
+ -   **接口**：
+     -   &#96;handleStorageChange()&#96;：当用户在 Popup 中切换状态时，立即在当前标签页应用或移除样式。
+     -   &#96;handleTabUpdate()&#96;：当新页面加载时，检查状态并决定是否注入样式。
+ -   **依赖**：&#96;chrome.tabs&#96;, &#96;chrome.scripting&#96;, &#96;chrome.storage&#96; APIs。
+ 
+ ### 3. Retro Stylesheet (retro.css)
+ -   **目的**：定义所有的“手术级”复古样式。
+ -   **核心选择器**：
+     -   &#96;button&#96;, &#96;input[type="button"]&#96;：3D 灰色凸起。
+     -   &#96;h1&#96;, &#96;h2&#96;, &#96;h3&#96;：Times New Roman 字体覆盖。
+     -   &#96;a&#96;：强制下划线与蓝色。
+     -   &#96;img&#96;：CSS 滤镜叠加。
+ 
+ ## 数据模型
+ 
+ ### 状态模型
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;json
+ {
+   "isEnabled": "boolean"  // 默认为 true
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## 错误处理
+ 
+ ### 错误场景
+ 1.  **场景 1：权限不足**
+     -   **处理**：在 &#96;manifest.json&#96; 中明确声明 &#96;scripting&#96; 和 &#96;storage&#96; 权限。
+     -   **用户影响**：如果权限配置不当，样式将无法注入。
+ 2.  **场景 2：样式冲突**
+     -   **处理**：使用极其具体且带有 &#96;!important&#96; 的选择器，并定期通过测试优化选择器。
+     -   **用户影响**：部分现代网页的高度复杂样式可能无法被完全覆盖。
+ 
+ ## 测试策略
+ 
+ ### 单元测试
+ -   测试 &#96;chrome.storage&#96; 的读取与写入逻辑是否正确。
+ 
+ ### 集成测试
+ -   验证从 Popup 切换状态后，Service Worker 是否能正确触发 &#96;chrome.scripting.insertCSS&#96;。
+ 
+ ### 端到端测试 (E2E)
+ -   在主流网站（如 Google, Baidu, Wikipedia）上运行插件，通过 &#96;cursor-browser-extension&#96; 验证按钮、文字和滚动条是否呈现复古视觉效果。
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="mcp" data-tool-name="mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation">
<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: spec-workflow - log-implementation: Record comprehensive implementation details for a completed task.

⚠️ CRITICAL: Artifacts are REQUIRED. This creates a searchable knowledge base that future AI agents use to discover existing code and avoid duplication.

# WHY DETAILED LOGGING MATTERS

Future AI agents (and future you) will use grep/ripgrep to search implementation logs before implementing new tasks. Complete logs prevent:
- ❌ Creating duplicate API endpoints
- ❌ Reimplementing existing components
- ❌ Duplicating utility functions and business logic
- ❌ Breaking established integration patterns

Incomplete logs = Duplicated code = Technical debt

# REQUIRED FIELDS

## artifacts (REQUIRED - Object)

Contains structured data about what was implemented. Must include relevant artifact types:

### apiEndpoints (array of API endpoint objects)
When new API endpoints are created/modified, document:
- method: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
- path: Route path (e.g., "/api/specs/:name/logs")
- purpose: What this endpoint does
- requestFormat: Request body/query params format (JSON schema or example)
- responseFormat: Response structure (JSON schema or example)
- location: File path and line number (e.g., "src/server.ts:245")

Example:
```
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
  "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
  "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
  "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
}
```

### components (array of component objects)
When reusable UI components are created, document:
- name: Component name
- type: Framework type (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- purpose: What the component does
- location: File path
- props: Props interface or type signature
- exports: What it exports (array of export names)

Example:
```
{
  "name": "LogsPage",
  "type": "React",
  "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
  "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
  "props": "{ specs: any[], selectedSpec: string, onSelect: (value: string) => void }",
  "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
}
```

### functions (array of function objects)
When utility functions are created, document:
- name: Function name
- purpose: What it does
- location: File path and line
- signature: Function signature (params and return type)
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "searchLogs",
  "purpose": "Search implementation logs by keyword",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts:156",
  "signature": "(searchTerm: string) => Promise<ImplementationLogEntry[]>",
  "isExported": true
}
```

### classes (array of class objects)
When classes are created, document:
- name: Class name
- purpose: What the class does
- location: File path
- methods: List of public methods
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
  "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
  "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
  "isExported": true
}
```

### integrations (array of integration objects)
Document how frontend connects to backend:
- description: How components connect to APIs
- frontendComponent: Which component initiates the connection
- backendEndpoint: Which API endpoint is called
- dataFlow: Describe the data flow (e.g., "User clicks → API call → State update → Re-render")

Example:
```
{
  "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
  "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
  "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
}
```

# GOOD EXAMPLE (Include ALL relevant artifacts)

Task: "Implemented logs dashboard with real-time updates"

```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Implemented real-time implementation logs dashboard with filtering, search, and WebSocket updates",
  "artifacts": {
    "apiEndpoints": [
      {
        "method": "GET",
        "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
        "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
        "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
        "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
        "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
      }
    ],
    "components": [
      {
        "name": "LogsPage",
        "type": "React",
        "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
        "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
        "props": "None (uses React Router params)",
        "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
      }
    ],
    "classes": [
      {
        "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
        "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
        "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
        "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
        "isExported": true
      }
    ],
    "integrations": [
      {
        "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
        "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
        "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
        "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
      }
    ]
  },
  "filesModified": ["src/dashboard/server.ts"],
  "filesCreated": ["src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx"],
  "statistics": { "linesAdded": 650, "linesRemoved": 15, "filesChanged": 2 }
}
```

# BAD EXAMPLE (Don't do this)

❌ Empty artifacts - Future agents learn nothing:
```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Added endpoint and page",
  "artifacts": {},
  "filesModified": ["server.ts"],
  "filesCreated": ["LogsPage.tsx"]
}
```

❌ Vague summary with no structured data:
```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Implemented features",
  "artifacts": {},
  "filesModified": ["server.ts", "app.tsx"]
}
```

1. After completing a task, review what you implemented

```diff
+ /* 
+    Y2K-ifier: Retro 2000s Stylesheet
+    Surgical transformation without affecting layout.
+ */
+ 
+ /* 1. 全局基础文字：模拟 MS Sans Serif 风格 */
+ body, p, span, li, td, input, textarea, select {
+     font-family: Arial, "MS Sans Serif", "Microsoft Sans Serif", sans-serif !important;
+     font-weight: normal !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 2. 标题样式：经典的 Times New Roman 与深蓝色 */
+ h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6 {
+     font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif !important;
+     color: #000080 !important; /* Classic Navy Blue */
+     text-transform: none !important;
+     letter-spacing: normal !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 3. 链接：复古的蓝色下划线与紫色访问状态 */
+ a {
+     color: #0000ee !important;
+     text-decoration: underline !important;
+ }
+ a:visited {
+     color: #551a8b !important;
+ }
+ a:hover {
+     color: #ff0000 !important; /* 悬停变红是不少老网站的习惯 */
+ }
+ 
+ /* 4. 按钮：经典的灰色 3D 凸起效果 */
+ button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], input[type="reset"], .btn {
+     background-color: #c0c0c0 !important;
+     border-top: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+     border-left: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+     border-bottom: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-right: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-radius: 0 !important;
+     padding: 3px 10px !important;
+     color: #000000 !important;
+     box-shadow: none !important;
+     text-shadow: none !important;
+     cursor: pointer !important;
+     font-size: 13px !important; /* 老按钮通常字比较小 */
+ }
+ 
+ button:active, input[type="button"]:active, input[type="submit"]:active {
+     border-top: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-left: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-bottom: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+     border-right: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 5. 图片：低保真滤镜与像素渲染 */
+ img {
+     filter: contrast(115%) sepia(15%) brightness(105%) !important;
+     image-rendering: pixelated !important;
+     border: 1px solid #808080 !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 6. 表单输入框：内陷效果 */
+ input[type="text"], input[type="password"], textarea, select {
+     background-color: #ffffff !important;
+     border-top: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-left: 2px solid #808080 !important;
+     border-bottom: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+     border-right: 2px solid #ffffff !important;
+     border-radius: 0 !important;
+     padding: 2px !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 7. 系统风格滚动条 (Webkit) */
+ ::-webkit-scrollbar {
+     width: 16px !important;
+     height: 16px !important;
+ }
+ ::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
+     background: #dfdfdf url('data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAIAAAACCAYAAABytg0kAAAAFElEQVQImWNkYGBoYGBgYmBgYAAAAAYAAfL0V74AAAAASUVORK5CYII=') repeat !important;
+ }
+ ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
+     background-color: #c0c0c0 !important;
+     border: 2px outset #ffffff !important;
+ }
+ ::-webkit-scrollbar-button {
+     background-color: #c0c0c0 !important;
+     border: 2px outset #ffffff !important;
+     display: block !important;
+ }
+ 
+ /* 8. 排除图标字体以防止乱码 */
+ [class*="icon"], [class*="fa-"], .material-icons, [style*="font-family: icon"], [style*="font-family: 'Font Awesome'"] {
+     font-family: inherit !important;
+ }
+ 
```

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: spec-workflow - log-implementation: Record comprehensive implementation details for a completed task.

⚠️ CRITICAL: Artifacts are REQUIRED. This creates a searchable knowledge base that future AI agents use to discover existing code and avoid duplication.

# WHY DETAILED LOGGING MATTERS

Future AI agents (and future you) will use grep/ripgrep to search implementation logs before implementing new tasks. Complete logs prevent:
- ❌ Creating duplicate API endpoints
- ❌ Reimplementing existing components
- ❌ Duplicating utility functions and business logic
- ❌ Breaking established integration patterns

Incomplete logs = Duplicated code = Technical debt

# REQUIRED FIELDS

## artifacts (REQUIRED - Object)

Contains structured data about what was implemented. Must include relevant artifact types:

### apiEndpoints (array of API endpoint objects)
When new API endpoints are created/modified, document:
- method: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
- path: Route path (e.g., "/api/specs/:name/logs")
- purpose: What this endpoint does
- requestFormat: Request body/query params format (JSON schema or example)
- responseFormat: Response structure (JSON schema or example)
- location: File path and line number (e.g., "src/server.ts:245")

Example:
```
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
  "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
  "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
  "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
}
```

### components (array of component objects)
When reusable UI components are created, document:
- name: Component name
- type: Framework type (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- purpose: What the component does
- location: File path
- props: Props interface or type signature
- exports: What it exports (array of export names)

Example:
```
{
  "name": "LogsPage",
  "type": "React",
  "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
  "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
  "props": "{ specs: any[], selectedSpec: string, onSelect: (value: string) => void }",
  "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
}
```

### functions (array of function objects)
When utility functions are created, document:
- name: Function name
- purpose: What it does
- location: File path and line
- signature: Function signature (params and return type)
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "searchLogs",
  "purpose": "Search implementation logs by keyword",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts:156",
  "signature": "(searchTerm: string) => Promise<ImplementationLogEntry[]>",
  "isExported": true
}
```

### classes (array of class objects)
When classes are created, document:
- name: Class name
- purpose: What the class does
- location: File path
- methods: List of public methods
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
  "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
  "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
  "isExported": true
}
```

### integrations (array of integration objects)
Document how frontend connects to backend:
- description: How components connect to APIs
- frontendComponent: Which component initiates the connection
- backendEndpoint: Which API endpoint is called
- dataFlow: Describe the data flow (e.g., "User clicks → API call → State update → Re-render")

Example:
```
{
  "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
  "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
  "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
}
```

```diff
- 
+ document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', async () =&gt; {
+     const toggle = document.getElementById('retroToggle');
+ 
+     // 1. 初始化：从存储中获取当前状态
+     const data = await chrome.storage.local.get('isEnabled');
+     toggle.checked = data.isEnabled !== false; // 默认为 true
+ 
+     // 2. 监听切换事件
+     toggle.addEventListener('change', async () =&gt; {
+         const newState = toggle.checked;
+         
+         // 3. 保存新状态
+         await chrome.storage.local.set({ isEnabled: newState });
+ 
+         // 4. 通知 Service Worker 立即更新当前标签页
+         chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ action: 'toggleRetro', state: newState });
+     });
+ });
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

```diff
@@ -1,6 +1,70 @@
- // Background service worker for Y2K-ifier
+ // Background Service Worker for Y2K-ifier
+ 
+ const RETRO_CSS_FILE = 'styles/retro.css';
+ 
+ // 1. 安装或更新时初始化状态
  chrome.runtime.onInstalled.addListener(() =&gt; {
-   chrome.storage.local.set({ isEnabled: true });
-   console.log('Y2K-ifier extension installed and enabled.');
+     chrome.storage.local.get(['isEnabled'], (result) =&gt; {
+         if (result.isEnabled === undefined) {
+             chrome.storage.local.set({ isEnabled: true });
+         }
+     });
+ });
+ 
+ // 2. 核心功能：向指定标签页注入或移除 CSS
+ async function updateTabStyle(tabId, isEnabled) {
+     if (!tabId) return;
+ 
+     try {
+         if (isEnabled) {
+             await chrome.scripting.insertCSS({
+                 target: { tabId: tabId },
+                 files: [RETRO_CSS_FILE]
+             });
+             console.log(&#96;Injected retro CSS into tab ${tabId}&#96;);
+         } else {
+             await chrome.scripting.removeCSS({
+                 target: { tabId: tabId },
+                 files: [RETRO_CSS_FILE]
+             });
+             console.log(&#96;Removed retro CSS from tab ${tabId}&#96;);
+         }
+     } catch (err) {
+         // 忽略一些无法注入的页面（如 chrome://, edge:// 等）
+         console.warn(&#96;Could not update style for tab ${tabId}:&#96;, err.message);
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ // 3. 监听存储变更（用户在 Popup 中切换开关）
+ chrome.storage.onChanged.addListener(async (changes, area) =&gt; {
+     if (area === 'local' &amp;&amp; changes.isEnabled) {
+         const newState = changes.isEnabled.newValue;
+         const tabs = await chrome.tabs.query({});
+         
+         // 更新所有标签页
+         for (const tab of tabs) {
+             updateTabStyle(tab.id, newState);
+         }
+     }
+ });
+ 
+ // 4. 监听标签页更新（用户导航到新页面）
+ chrome.tabs.onUpdated.addListener(async (tabId, changeInfo, tab) =&gt; {
+     if (changeInfo.status === 'loading') {
+         const data = await chrome.storage.local.get('isEnabled');
+         const isEnabled = data.isEnabled !== false;
+         
+         if (isEnabled) {
+             updateTabStyle(tabId, true);
+         }
+     }
+ });
+ 
+ // 5. 监听来自 Popup 的显式消息（可选，增强即时性）
+ chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener((request, sender, sendResponse) =&gt; {
+     if (request.action === 'toggleRetro') {
+         // 实际上 storage.onChanged 已经覆盖了这种情况
+         console.log('Explicit toggle received:', request.state);
+     }
  });
  
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="mcp" data-tool-name="mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation">
<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: spec-workflow - log-implementation: Record comprehensive implementation details for a completed task.

⚠️ CRITICAL: Artifacts are REQUIRED. This creates a searchable knowledge base that future AI agents use to discover existing code and avoid duplication.

# WHY DETAILED LOGGING MATTERS

Future AI agents (and future you) will use grep/ripgrep to search implementation logs before implementing new tasks. Complete logs prevent:
- ❌ Creating duplicate API endpoints
- ❌ Reimplementing existing components
- ❌ Duplicating utility functions and business logic
- ❌ Breaking established integration patterns

Incomplete logs = Duplicated code = Technical debt

# REQUIRED FIELDS

## artifacts (REQUIRED - Object)

Contains structured data about what was implemented. Must include relevant artifact types:

### apiEndpoints (array of API endpoint objects)
When new API endpoints are created/modified, document:
- method: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
- path: Route path (e.g., "/api/specs/:name/logs")
- purpose: What this endpoint does
- requestFormat: Request body/query params format (JSON schema or example)
- responseFormat: Response structure (JSON schema or example)
- location: File path and line number (e.g., "src/server.ts:245")

Example:
```
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
  "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
  "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
  "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
}
```

### components (array of component objects)
When reusable UI components are created, document:
- name: Component name
- type: Framework type (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- purpose: What the component does
- location: File path
- props: Props interface or type signature
- exports: What it exports (array of export names)

Example:
```
{
  "name": "LogsPage",
  "type": "React",
  "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
  "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
  "props": "{ specs: any[], selectedSpec: string, onSelect: (value: string) => void }",
  "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
}
```

### functions (array of function objects)
When utility functions are created, document:
- name: Function name
- purpose: What it does
- location: File path and line
- signature: Function signature (params and return type)
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "searchLogs",
  "purpose": "Search implementation logs by keyword",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts:156",
  "signature": "(searchTerm: string) => Promise<ImplementationLogEntry[]>",
  "isExported": true
}
```

### classes (array of class objects)
When classes are created, document:
- name: Class name
- purpose: What the class does
- location: File path
- methods: List of public methods
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
  "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
  "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
  "isExported": true
}
```

### integrations (array of integration objects)
Document how frontend connects to backend:
- description: How components connect to APIs
- frontendComponent: Which component initiates the connection
- backendEndpoint: Which API endpoint is called
- dataFlow: Describe the data flow (e.g., "User clicks → API call → State update → Re-render")

Example:
```
{
  "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
  "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
  "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
}
```

```diff
- 
+ # OpenMemory - Y2K-ifier
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ **Y2K-ifier** 是一款 Google Chrome 扩展插件（Manifest V3），通过“手术级”视觉重塑将现代网页转换为 2000 年代的复古风格。
+ 
+ ## Architecture
+ - **Manifest V3**: 使用 Service Worker (&#96;background.js&#96;) 管理全局状态。
+ - **Surgical CSS Injection**: 利用 &#96;chrome.scripting&#96; API 在不破坏布局的前提下注入 &#96;retro.css&#96;。
+ - **Persistent Storage**: 使用 &#96;chrome.storage.local&#96; 持久化“复古模式”开关状态。
+ - **Retro UI**: Popup 界面采用 Windows 2000 风格设计。
+ 
+ ## User Defined Namespaces
+ - frontend: 包含 Popup UI 和 CSS 样式逻辑。
+ - extension: 包含 Manifest 配置和 Service Worker 逻辑。
+ 
+ ## Components
+ ### [Component] - Popup UI
+ - **Location**: &#96;popup/&#96;
+ - **Purpose**: 提供用户控制开关，采用 Win2000 风格。
+ - **Services**: &#96;chrome.storage&#96;, &#96;chrome.runtime&#96;.
+ 
+ ### [Component] - Retro Stylesheet
+ - **Location**: &#96;styles/retro.css&#96;
+ - **Purpose**: 定义核心视觉变换（3D 按钮、衬线标题、像素化图片、复古滚动条）。
+ 
+ ## Patterns
+ - **Surgical Injection**: 仅修改装饰性 CSS 属性（border, color, font, filter），避免修改 layout 属性（width, height, flex）。
+ - **State-driven Injection**: Service Worker 监听存储和标签页更新，动态同步 CSS 状态。
+ 
```

*Parameters*:
  * content: # Implementation: Y2K-ifier Retro Chrome Extension

## Purpose
Developed a Chrome Extension to transform modern web pages into a 2000s retro style using surgical CSS injection.

## Key Decisions
- **Manifest V3**: Used for modern browser compatibility and performance.
- **Surgical CSS**: Focused on decoration (3D borders, fonts, filters) to avoid breaking modern site layouts.
- **Service Worker**: Used to manage dynamic injection across all tabs based on a central state.
- **Storage API**: `chrome.storage.local` ensures the user's preference is remembered.

## Components
- `manifest.json`: Core configuration.
- `background.js`: Injection logic and state management.
- `popup/`: Win2000 style UI for toggling the mode.
- `styles/retro.css`: The "soul" of the extension with detailed retro styling rules.

## Patterns
- Used `!important` in CSS to ensure overrides on complex modern sites.
- Targeted `role="button"` and common class patterns for better coverage.
- Excluded icon fonts to maintain site usability.

恭喜！**Y2K-ifier** 插件的开发已经全部完成。

这是一个纯前端的 Google Chrome 扩展插件（Manifest V3），它通过“手术级”的 CSS 注入技术，在不破坏现代网页布局的前提下，精准地将视觉风格回溯到 2000 年代。

### 已完成的开发工作：
1.  **项目初始化**：配置了 Manifest V3，声明了 `scripting`、`storage` 和 `activeTab` 权限。
2.  **核心复古样式表 (`styles/retro.css`)**：
    *   **按钮**：实现了经典的灰色 3D 凸起效果（outset 边框）。
    *   **文字**：标题强制使用 Times New Roman，正文使用 Arial，链接带蓝色下划线。
    *   **图片**：添加了像素化滤镜（pixelated rendering）和轻微的复古色调。
    *   **滚动条**：完全重塑为 Windows 2000 风格的灰色方块。
3.  **用户交互界面 (`popup/`)**：
    *   打造了一个 **Windows 2000 风格的弹出窗口**，带有经典的标题栏和控制开关。
    *   集成了 `chrome.storage.local`，能够持久化保存用户的开关状态。

<details>
          <summary>Tool use: **mcp_spec-workflow_log-implementation**</summary>
      
*Called tool*: spec-workflow - log-implementation: Record comprehensive implementation details for a completed task.

⚠️ CRITICAL: Artifacts are REQUIRED. This creates a searchable knowledge base that future AI agents use to discover existing code and avoid duplication.

# WHY DETAILED LOGGING MATTERS

Future AI agents (and future you) will use grep/ripgrep to search implementation logs before implementing new tasks. Complete logs prevent:
- ❌ Creating duplicate API endpoints
- ❌ Reimplementing existing components
- ❌ Duplicating utility functions and business logic
- ❌ Breaking established integration patterns

Incomplete logs = Duplicated code = Technical debt

# REQUIRED FIELDS

## artifacts (REQUIRED - Object)

Contains structured data about what was implemented. Must include relevant artifact types:

### apiEndpoints (array of API endpoint objects)
When new API endpoints are created/modified, document:
- method: HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
- path: Route path (e.g., "/api/specs/:name/logs")
- purpose: What this endpoint does
- requestFormat: Request body/query params format (JSON schema or example)
- responseFormat: Response structure (JSON schema or example)
- location: File path and line number (e.g., "src/server.ts:245")

Example:
```
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
  "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
  "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
  "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
}
```

### components (array of component objects)
When reusable UI components are created, document:
- name: Component name
- type: Framework type (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- purpose: What the component does
- location: File path
- props: Props interface or type signature
- exports: What it exports (array of export names)

Example:
```
{
  "name": "LogsPage",
  "type": "React",
  "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
  "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
  "props": "{ specs: any[], selectedSpec: string, onSelect: (value: string) => void }",
  "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
}
```

### functions (array of function objects)
When utility functions are created, document:
- name: Function name
- purpose: What it does
- location: File path and line
- signature: Function signature (params and return type)
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "searchLogs",
  "purpose": "Search implementation logs by keyword",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts:156",
  "signature": "(searchTerm: string) => Promise<ImplementationLogEntry[]>",
  "isExported": true
}
```

### classes (array of class objects)
When classes are created, document:
- name: Class name
- purpose: What the class does
- location: File path
- methods: List of public methods
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
  "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
  "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
  "isExported": true
}
```

### integrations (array of integration objects)
Document how frontend connects to backend:
- description: How components connect to APIs
- frontendComponent: Which component initiates the connection
- backendEndpoint: Which API endpoint is called
- dataFlow: Describe the data flow (e.g., "User clicks → API call → State update → Re-render")

Example:
```
{
  "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
  "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
  "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
}
```

# GOOD EXAMPLE (Include ALL relevant artifacts)

Task: "Implemented logs dashboard with real-time updates"

```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Implemented real-time implementation logs dashboard with filtering, search, and WebSocket updates",
  "artifacts": {
    "apiEndpoints": [
      {
        "method": "GET",
        "path": "/api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
        "purpose": "Retrieve implementation logs with optional filtering",
        "requestFormat": "Query params: taskId (string, optional), search (string, optional)",
        "responseFormat": "{ entries: ImplementationLogEntry[] }",
        "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
      }
    ],
    "components": [
      {
        "name": "LogsPage",
        "type": "React",
        "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
        "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
        "props": "None (uses React Router params)",
        "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
      }
    ],
    "classes": [
      {
        "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
        "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
        "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
        "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
        "isExported": true
      }
    ],
    "integrations": [
      {
        "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
        "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
        "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
        "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
      }
    ]
  },
  "filesModified": ["src/dashboard/server.ts"],
  "filesCreated": ["src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx"],
  "statistics": { "linesAdded": 650, "linesRemoved": 15, "filesChanged": 2 }
}
```

# BAD EXAMPLE (Don't do this)

❌ Empty artifacts - Future agents learn nothing:
```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Added endpoint and page",
  "artifacts": {},
  "filesModified": ["server.ts"],
  "filesCreated": ["LogsPage.tsx"]
}
```

❌ Vague summary with no structured data:
```json
{
  "taskId": "2.3",
  "summary": "Implemented features",
  "artifacts": {},
  "filesModified": ["server.ts", "app.tsx"]
}
```

1. After completing a task, review what you implemented
2. Identify all artifacts (APIs, components, functions, classes, integrations)
3. Document each with full details and locations

```
  "location": "src/dashboard/server.ts:245"
}
```

### components (array of component objects)
When reusable UI components are created, document:
- name: Component name
- type: Framework type (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.)
- purpose: What the component does
- location: File path
- props: Props interface or type signature
- exports: What it exports (array of export names)

Example:
```
{
  "name": "LogsPage",
  "type": "React",
  "purpose": "Main dashboard page for viewing implementation logs with search and filtering",
  "location": "src/modules/pages/LogsPage.tsx",
  "props": "{ specs: any[], selectedSpec: string, onSelect: (value: string) => void }",
  "exports": ["LogsPage (default)"]
}
```

### functions (array of function objects)
When utility functions are created, document:
- name: Function name
- purpose: What it does
- location: File path and line
- signature: Function signature (params and return type)
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "searchLogs",
  "purpose": "Search implementation logs by keyword",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts:156",
  "signature": "(searchTerm: string) => Promise<ImplementationLogEntry[]>",
  "isExported": true
}
```

### classes (array of class objects)
When classes are created, document:
- name: Class name
- purpose: What the class does
- location: File path
- methods: List of public methods
- isExported: Whether it can be imported

Example:
```
{
  "name": "ImplementationLogManager",
  "purpose": "Manages CRUD operations for implementation logs",
  "location": "src/dashboard/implementation-log-manager.ts",
  "methods": ["loadLog", "addLogEntry", "getAllLogs", "searchLogs", "getTaskStats"],
  "isExported": true
}
```

### integrations (array of integration objects)
Document how frontend connects to backend:
- description: How components connect to APIs
- frontendComponent: Which component initiates the connection
- backendEndpoint: Which API endpoint is called
- dataFlow: Describe the data flow (e.g., "User clicks → API call → State update → Re-render")

Example:
```
{
  "description": "LogsPage fetches logs via REST API and subscribes to WebSocket for real-time updates",
  "frontendComponent": "LogsPage",
  "backendEndpoint": "GET /api/specs/:name/implementation-log",
  "dataFlow": "Component mount → API fetch → Display logs → WebSocket subscription → Real-time updates on new entries"
}
```

出现 "An unknown error occurred when fetching the script" 错误，通常是由于 Chrome 扩展的 **Service Worker (background.js) 注册失败** 导致的。

这通常由以下三个原因引起：
1.  **文件缺失**：如果在 `manifest.json` 中引用了 `icons/icon16.png` 等文件，但文件夹中还没有这些 PNG 文件，Chrome 会直接报错。
2.  **语法或异步监听器问题**：在某些 Chrome 版本中，直接将 `async` 函数作为监听器（如 `onUpdated.addListener(async ...)`）可能会导致注册不稳定。
3.  **缓存问题**：扩展程序更新后没有彻底重新加载。

### 我已经为您做了以下优化：
1.  **重构了 `background.js`**：
    *   将监听器改回了非 `async` 形式，改在函数体内部处理异步逻辑，这在 Chrome 扩展中更稳定。
    *   增加了对受保护页面（如 `chrome://` 页面）的检查，防止脚本在这些禁止注入的页面上报错。
    *   将注入时机从 `loading` 改为了 `complete`，确保页面结构加载完成后再应用复古样式。
2.  **增加了错误捕获**：即使某个标签页注入失败，也不会影响整个 Service Worker 的运行。

### 您需要检查的操作：
1.  **确认 PNG 图标是否存在**：请务必确认 `icons/` 文件夹下已经有了 `icon16.png`, `icon48.png`, `icon128.png` 这三个文件。如果它们还没到位，请先将 SVG 转换并保存为 PNG（或者临时在 `manifest.json` 中把图片后缀改回 `.svg` 测试，虽然 Chrome 最终发布需要 PNG）。
2.  **彻底重新加载插件**：
    *   在 `chrome://extensions/` 页面。
    *   找到 Y2K-ifier。
    *   点击右下角的 **刷新图标 (Update/Reload)**。
    *   点击 **"Service Worker"** 蓝色链接，看控制台是否还有错误。

**您可以先尝试刷新插件，如果还是报错，请告诉我，我们继续排查！**

我已经进一步强化了图片“去圆角”的逻辑。

### 核心改进：
1.  **多维度清除**：除了 `border-radius: 0`，我还添加了 `clip-path: none !important` 和 `mask-image: none !important`。这能防止某些现代网页使用“剪切路径”或“蒙版”技术来强行给图片切出圆角。
2.  **扩大目标范围**：现在不仅针对 `img` 标签，还覆盖了 `svg` 标签以及所有带有 `image` 或 `img` 类名的元素，确保万无一失。
3.  **渲染优化**：添加了针对不同浏览器的 `crisp-edges` 属性，让图片在去圆角的同时，边缘更加锐利，像素感更强。
4.  **消除阴影**：去除了图片可能携带的 `box-shadow`，防止阴影造成的视觉模糊。

现在的图片应该是绝对的“直角矩形”了。您可以刷新页面观察效果！如果有任何顽固的圆角依然存在，请告诉我具体的网址，我会继续针对性优化。

This limitation greatly influenced the design choices of the era.\n\n### Resolution Constraints:\n\nMonitors with lower resolutions were the norm. Designers faced the challenge of creating visually appealing websites within the constraints of 800×600 pixels. While they added flair, they also tested the patience of users on slower connections.\n\n### Splash Pages:\n\nMany websites embraced splash pages, often adorned with “Enter” buttons. Splash pages were the precursor to loading pages of today. These introductory pages aimed to create a cinematic experience but were more of an impediment to users seeking swift access.\n\n### Colourful Chaos:\n\nBright and contrasting colours defined the era. Neon greens, electric blues, and hot pinks adorned backgrounds and text alike.\n\n### Pixelated GIFs:\n\nPixelated GIFs were the go-to for adding visual interest.     "text": "About web badges\n\nToggle search panel\n\n### Loading...\n\nPreparing nearly 4,000 web badges, please be patient!\n\n### A Brief History\n\nDo you remember these tiny 80x15 buttons that used to adorn websites all over the internet long ago?  **Web badges** were very popular when the internet was younger, when web standards had not yet matured and search engines were not yet well established.  Also known as _antipixel buttons_ or _brilliant buttons_, these **web badges** gained popularity especially amongst bloggers as a way to provide a great deal of information about a website and its author at just a quick glance.\n\nDuring a time before web standards and responsive web design existed, **web badges** were first mainly used to help identify with what browser or at what resolution a site was best viewed, or to show that a site complied with those early web standards as they emerged.  **Web badges** were also commonly used for syndication and sharing Atom or RSS feeds.\n\nBefore there were advanced search engines to scour the web for us, many bloggers used **web badges** to link to directories where their site was listed, or as part of a webring they belonged to.  A webring is simply a group of websites around a common subject, where the site owners all agree to link to each other to collectively increase their online exposure.  Many bloggers would also use these badges to share their blogroll, or a curated list of their favorite and most frequented websites on the internet.\n\nFor a time, **web badges** exploded in popularity and were used for many other different purposes!  Some badges advertised the platform the site was built on, the language it was built with, the editor used to build it, the operating system running it, or the provider hosting it.  Some badges shared personal information about the author, such as geographical location, political or religious beliefs, what games they play, what sports teams they follow, what music they listen to, or what food they eat.  There were of course many joke and meme badges created as well.\n\n### The Next Chapter\n\n### What happened to web badges?\n\nSo what happened to **web badges** and why did they fall out of style?  The improvements made to major search engines allow us to find information online quickly and easily today, and combined with the evolution of cross compatible responsive web design best practices, most of the functionality that web badges provided has now been rendered obsolete.  While these badges were once practically ubiquitous across blogs long ago, most of this collection was actually stolen from the depths of the [internet archives](https://web.archive.org/web/20080302152605/http://gtmcknight.com/buttons/), as it sadly seems they have become a nearly forgotten gem of early internet history.  I made this website to _save **web badges**_ and bring them back into popularity by reminding everyone how cool they were with this huge collection of nearly 4,000 examples!",
    "title": "Web Badges World | The ultimate archive of 80x15 pixel button art",
    "score": null,
    "__typename": "WebSearchResult"
  },

    "text": "[Skip to Content](https://www.zachleat.com/web/malarquee-bringing-back-the-marquee#skiplink-content)\n\n# maLArquee, Bringing Back the Marquee\n\n_August 20, 2007_\n\nWhat did you spend your Saturday afternoon on? Did you kick up your feet in your hammock with a nice glass of lemonade in the shade of your favorite tree and read the HTML specification? Me too! Who knew that we’d have so much in common? Since you’re obviously like me, you’ve probably wondered to yourself: where did the marquee tag go? Why isn’t the internet graced with scrolling text gently flowing like a babbling brook across the pixels of your web browser?     "text": "[Skip to content](https://alistapart.com/article/slidingdoors/#content)\n\n**A note from the editors:** While brilliant for its time, this article no longer reflects modern best practices.\n\nA rarely discussed advantage of CSS is the ability to _layer_ background images, allowing them to _slide_ over each other to create certain effects. CSS2’s current state requires a separate HTML element for each background image. In many cases, typical markup for common interface components has already provided several elements for our use.\n\nArticle Continues Below\n\nArticle Continues Below\n\nOne of those cases is tabbed navigation. It’s time to take back control over the tabs which are continually growing in popularity as a primary means of site navigation. Now that CSS is widely supported, we can crank up the quality and appearance of the tabs on our sites. You’re most likely aware that CSS can be used to [tame a plain unordered list](https://alistapart.com/articles/taminglists/). Maybe you’ve even seen lists styled as tabs, looking something like this:\n\n![[Ordinary example of CSS-based tabs, using flat colors and squared-off corners.]](https://i0.wp.com/alistapart.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/07/tabex1.gif?resize=228%2C34&ssl=1)\n\nWhat if we could take **the exact same markup** from the tabs above, and turn them into something like this:\n\n![[Stylized tabs using rounded corners and subtle three-dimensional shading.]](https://i0.wp.com/alistapart.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/07/tabex2.gif?resize=228%2C35&ssl=1)\n\nWith simple styling, **we can**.\n\n## Where’s the Innovation? [\\#section2](https://alistapart.com/article/slidingdoors/\\#section2)\n\nMany of the CSS-based tabs I’ve seen suffer from the same generic features: blocky rectangles of color, maybe an outline, a border disappears for the current tab, a color changes for the hover state. Is this all CSS can offer us? A bunch of boxes and flat colors?\n\nPrior to a more widespread adoption of CSS, we started seeing a lot of innovation in navigation design. Creative shapes, masterful color blending, and mimicry of physical interfaces from the real world. But these designs often relied heavily on a complex construction of text-embedded images, or were wrapped with multiple nested tables.
